Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

__(A)__ biodiversity worldwide is incredibly challenging; national monitoring programmes differ widely, the majority of collected data is erratic and little is __(B)__ publicly. But scientists may have found a surprising solution: the filters already used __(C)__ the world to monitor air pollution. These devices have for decades been unintentionally capturing large amounts of environmental DNA from animals and plants. Scientists say this could be used to help us __(D)__ past, as well as future, changes in biodiversity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank B.
spmock001.explanation:
The sentence with the blank talks about the data regarding our biodiversity. The blank requires a verb which is qualified by the adverb 'publicly'. The verb 'sold' doesn't fit here as this data is collected for research purposes, not for a business. Similarly, the phrases 'corrected publicly' and 'calculated publicly' are incorrect. Researchers are not going to correct or calculate this data publicly. So, they are also eliminated. Among the given options, 'shared' is the correct choice.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

__(A)__ biodiversity worldwide is incredibly challenging; national monitoring programmes differ widely, the majority of collected data is erratic and little is __(B)__ publicly. But scientists may have found a surprising solution: the filters already used __(C)__ the world to monitor air pollution. These devices have for decades been unintentionally capturing large amounts of environmental DNA from animals and plants. Scientists say this could be used to help us __(D)__ past, as well as future, changes in biodiversity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank C.
spmock001.explanation:
The blank requires a preposition. Among the given options, the sentence states that devices that are used to monitor air pollution can be used to monitor biodiversity. 'Along' is used with a straight path, river, etc. So, it is eliminated. 'Over' is used to convey if something is above or higher than something else. It doesn't fit in the given sentence. Between the two remaining options, 'around' is the correct choice. To monitor air pollution, we need to place the device in every part of the world and not in a particular place. So, 'in' is eliminated.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the ______ (A) part of the last century there lived a man of science, an eminent proficient in every branch of natural philosophy, ______ (B) not long before our story opens had made the experience of a spiritual affinity more attractive than any chemical one. He had left his laboratory to the care of an assistant, cleared his fine countenance from the furnace smoke, ______ (C) the stain of acids from his fingers, and persuaded a beautiful woman to become his wife. In those days when the comparatively recent ________ (D) of electricity and other kindred mysteries of Nature seemed to open paths into the region of miracle, it was not unusual for the love of science to rival the love of a woman in its depth and absorbing energy.

Which of the following words can fill in the blank A?
spmock001.explanation:
The blank requires an adjective that qualifies the noun 'part' and denotes the specific part of the last century. 'Fast' (moving or capable of moving at high speed), 'normal' (usual, typical, or expected) and 'lush' (growing luxuriantly) do not denote the time of the century that is mentioned in the sentence and so, they are negated. 'Latter' (occurring or situated nearer to the end of something than to the beginning) is the word that matches the context of the sentence and denotes time as per the requirement of the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Qualifiers: A word or phrase that limits the meaning of another word or phrase or makes it less general. 'Adverbs' and 'adjectives' are qualifiers.

He had left his laboratory to the care of an assistant, cleared his fine countenance from the furnace smoke, ______ (C) the stain of acids from his fingers, and persuaded a beautiful woman to become his wife. In those days when the comparatively recent ________ (D) of electricity and other kindred mysteries of Nature seemed to open paths into the region of miracle, it was not unusual for the love of science to rival the love of a woman in its depth and absorbing energy.

Which of the following words can fill in the blank B?
spmock001.explanation:
The blank requires a relative pronoun that denotes the noun 'a man of science' that is also the subject of the sentence. 'Whose' denotes the possession of a person, 'which' is not used for humans and 'whom' is used to refer to the object and so, these options are negated. 'Who' is the pronoun that denotes the person, as required in the sentence and can thus fill the given blank.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

The middle four sentences have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your answer accordingly.

S1: The cosmos, with its mystery governed by immutable laws of poetic precision, staggered her imagination

S6:. And so, at seventeen, she founded a small school of her own.

P : by fifteen, she had mastered higher mathematics

Q : which she supplemented with an ardent love of poetry

R : further to offer her in the way of higher education for a woman

S : no institution - not on the island, not on the globe - had anything

The proper sequence should be
spmock001.explanation:
The first and the last sentence are fixed. We need to arrange PQRS in a way that the arrangement is meaningful and grammatically correct.

The last sentence (S6) mentions that 'so, she opened her own school'. The use of 'so' gives us a hint that the reason for her opening her own school must have been mentioned somewhere and it should precede the last sentence. The reason is mentioned in SR in that order; the reason being that no institution had anything to offer her. Option C satisfies this criterion. And PQSR is a meaningful sentence arrangement. Option C is the correct answer.

spmock001.word:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This profound philosophy treats breakage and repair as an integral part of the history of an object, rather than as something to be shamefully disguised.

B. Kintsugi is the exquisite Japanese art of repairing broken pottery by mending the areas of breakage with lacquer dusted or mixed with powdered gold or silver.

C. Consequently, the repaired ceramic piece is often considered more beautiful and valuable than the original, as it proudly showcases its scars as a mark of resilience.

D. Instead of attempting to hide the cracks, this unique method deliberately highlights them, celebrating imperfection as a beautiful part of the object's unique journey through time.
spmock001.explanation:
The correct sequence is BADC. Sentence B serves as the ideal introduction by defining the subject, "Kintsugi," and explaining the basic technique. Sentence A builds upon this by explaining the "profound philosophy" behind the art form mentioned in B. Sentence D elaborates on "this unique method" by contrasting it with typical repair, emphasizing how it "deliberately highlights" the cracks, which directly follows the philosophical point in A. Sentence C, with its transition word "Consequently," provides the logical conclusion, explaining the result of this artistic and philosophical approach, that the repaired piece becomes more beautiful.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

spmock001.word:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

She bought a new ________ of stylish sunglasses for her upcoming vacation.
spmock001.explanation:
The sentence refers to the purchase of sunglasses, which typically come as a set of two connected lenses. The phrase "a new ________ of stylish sunglasses" suggests the missing word is a noun that quantifies or describes how sunglasses are grouped.

The required part of speech is a noun, because it follows the adjective "new" and precedes the prepositional phrase "of stylish sunglasses," forming a noun phrase that is the object of "bought." The noun must logically connect with items that come in twos, like sunglasses.

Option b) pair is a noun. It refers to a set of two things used together or regarded as a unit, such as a pair of shoes or, in this case, sunglasses. This fits grammatically and aligns logically with how sunglasses are sold and described.

Option a) pare is a verb, meaning to trim (something) by cutting away its outer edges. It is not a noun and is contextually incorrect.

Option c) pear is a noun, referring to a type of fruit. It is contextually unrelated to sunglasses.

Option d) pier is a noun, meaning a structure leading out from the shore into a body of water. It is contextually inappropriate for describing sunglasses.

So, the complete sentence is: She bought a new pair of stylish sunglasses for her upcoming vacation.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

spmock001.word:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.

Is Savita is joining us for lunch today?
options: Is Savita joining us for lunch today?
Savita is joined us for lunch today?
Savita joining us for lunch today?
Are Savita joining us for lunch today?
spmock001.explanation:
An interrogative sentence is given in the question. Here, the helping verb ('is') should be used before the subject.

So, 'is' after 'Savita' makes the sentence erroneous.

Remove the second helping verb 'is' from the sentence to make it error-free.

The sentence in option (a) rectifies this error.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Option (b) is incorrect because the helping verb is used after the subject, which is incorrect for an interrogative sentence.

Option (c) is incorrect because of the absence of the helping verb 'is'.

Option (d) is incorrect because the plural verb 'are' is used for singular noun 'Savita'. This is a violation of subject-verb agreement.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

One of the formats of Direct Speech is:

Subject + will/shall + V1 + object.

He said, "I will go to Kolkata on Friday" (Direct Speech)

Among the given options, only (b) matches with required format. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

spmock001.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: People in different parts of India
have their own distinct habits when
it comes to marriages and festivals.
No Error
spmock001.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “habits” with “customs”.

Rule / Concept: Habit vs. Custom

While both words refer to repeated actions, their application depends on the subject performing the action:

-Habit (Individual): Refers to a settled or regular tendency or practice, especially one that is hard to give up. It belongs to a single person.

Example: Smoking is a bad habit.

-Custom (Group/Society): Refers to a traditional and widely accepted way of behaving or doing something that is specific to a particular society, place, or time.

Example: It is a Japanese custom to bow when greeting.

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the subject is "People in different parts of India" (a collective society or group). Marriages and festivals are not individual behavioral quirks; they are social traditions and rituals established by a culture. Therefore, the word "habits" is logically incorrect and should be replaced by "customs."

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 - He has a habit of waking up at 5 AM every day. (Individual action)

Example 2 - The custom of dowry is considered a social evil. (Social practice)

Example 3 - Every country has its own unique customs and traditions.

spmock001.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

He said to the mechanic, "Will you have the car ready by tomorrow morning?"
options: He asked the mechanic if he would have the car ready by the next morning.
He told the mechanic if he will have the car ready for the next morning.
He asked the mechanic if he will have the car ready by the previous morning.
He said the mechanic whether he would has the car ready by the following morning.
spmock001.explanation:
The original sentence is a question in direct speech. In reported speech, a question beginning with "Will" changes to "if/whether" and the verb shifts to the conditional "would." The phrase "tomorrow morning" becomes "the next morning" to reflect the time shift in reported speech. Option (a) correctly applies these rules: "asked" indicates a question, "if" introduces the reported question, and "would have" is the correct verb form. The other options contain grammatical errors or incorrect time references.

Option b: He told the mechanic if he will have the car ready for the next morning. "Told" is incorrect for a question (questions use "asked"). Additionally, "will" should be "would" in reported speech, and "for the next morning" is less precise than "by the next morning."

Option c: He asked the mechanic if he will have the car ready by the previous morning. "Will" should be "would" in reported speech, and "previous morning" is incorrect, as "tomorrow morning" should become "the next morning" in the context of reported speech.

Option d: He said the mechanic whether he would has the car ready by the following morning. "Said" is incorrect for a question (should be "asked"), "would has" is grammatically incorrect (should be "would have"), and the structure is awkward.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

spmock001.word:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the sentence that is error free from the given options.

He loves to plough weed and decorating his garden with exotic plants.
options: He loves to plough weed and decorate his garden with exotic plants.
He loves to plough weeding and decorating his garden with exotic plants.
He loves ploughing to weed and to decorating his garden with exotic plants.
He loves to ploughing weed and decorating his garden with exotic plants.
spmock001.explanation:
In the given sentence, the -ing form of the verb 'decorating' is incorrectly used along with the infinitive marker 'to'. Among the options, only option (a), 'He loves to plough weed and decorate his garden with exotic plants', has the correct base form of verb 'decorate' which agrees with the other verb form (plough). All the remaining options have the -ing form of verbs along with the infinitive marker 'to' which makes them grammatically incorrect and are thus negated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

spmock001.word:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow:

King Krishnadevaraya loved horses and had a collection of some of the best breeds of horses in his stable. Once a horse trader from Arabia came to the court of Krishnadevaraya and told him that he had some very good breed of Arabian horses for sale. He invited the King to see the horse that he had brought with him and told him that if he liked it, he would send for the other horses too. The King loved the horse and told him that he would like all his horses. The King paid him 5000 gold coins as an advance, and the trader promised that he would return with the other horses in 2 days before leaving.

Two days passed by, then two weeks and still, the trader did not return. The King got more and more anxious. One evening, to relax his mind, he went to take a stroll in the garden. There he saw Tenali Raman writing down something on a paper. The King went up to him and asked what he was writing. He did not get an answer. The King further quizzed him. Tenali then looked up and told the King that he was writing down the names of the biggest fools of the Vijayanagar Kingdom.

The King took the paper from him and saw his name written at the top. He was furious with Tenali and asked for an explanation. To that, Tenali replied that any man who gives away 5000 gold coins to a total stranger is a fool. The King then asked Tenali what if he returned with the horses; to which Tenali said then, in that case, that man would be a fool. He would then write down the trader's name instead of the king's.

Why did Tenali Raman initially write the King's name at the top of his list?
options: Because the King had been fooled by the trader's promise.
Because the King was not trustworthy.
Because the King had failed to pay the full price for the horses.
Because the King did not seek advice from his ministers.
spmock001.explanation: As mentioned in the story, Tenali remarks, "any man who gives away 5000 gold coins to a total stranger is a fool." (Paragraph 3) This explains why Tenali considered the King to be a fool for trusting the trader without first receiving the horses, which justifies the placement of the King's name at the top of the list. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The chef had prepared all the dishes before the guests arrived.
options: All the dishes were prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
All the dishes have been prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
All the dishes had been prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
All the dishes are prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.
spmock002.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice ("The chef") is changed into the object of the Passive Voice ("by the chef"). Also, the object of the Active Voice ("all the dishes") is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form ['been'] of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + had + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arya had bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

A new horse had been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice:

· (a) uses simple past ("were prepared")

· (b) uses present perfect ("have been prepared")

· (d) uses simple present ("are prepared")

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): All the dishes had been prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

spmock002.explanation:
The correct option is b).

This sentence correctly uses the passive voice of the simple past tense ("were engineered"). The passive is required because the subject ("aqueducts") is the receiver of the action (engineered). The plural subject "aqueducts" correctly pairs with the plural verb "were."

· Option (a): This has a subject-verb agreement error. The plural subject "aqueducts" requires the plural verb "were," not the singular verb "was."

· Option (c): This is grammatically incorrect. The passive voice requires the past participle ("engineered"), not the base form "engineer."

· Option (d): This is an incorrect passive construction. The past perfect passive would be "had been engineered."

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The captain said to the sailors, "If the wind stays strong, we will reach the shore by midnight."
options: The captain told the sailors that if the wind stays strong, they will reach the shore by midnight.
The captain told the sailors that if the wind stayed strong, they would reach the shore by midnight.
The captain told the sailors that if the wind had stayed strong, they would have reached the shore by midnight.
The captain told the sailors that if the wind stayed strong, we will reach the shore by midnight.
spmock002.explanation:
The correct answer is Option B: The captain told the sailors that if the wind stayed strong, they would reach the shore by midnight.

Key Points

  • The Conditional Shift: the Simple Present ("stays") shifts to Simple Past ("stayed") because the reporting verb "said" is in the past.

  • Modal Conversion: The future "will" must be converted into "would" to maintain the sequence of tenses.

  • Reporting Verb: "said to" correctly changes to "told" because there is an object ("the sailors").

  • Pronoun Change: The first-person plural "we" changes to "they" because the captain is reporting the action of the group to someone else.

  • Eliminating Incorrect Options:

    • Option A is wrong because it fails to change the tense.

    • Option C is a "Type 3" conditional trap (Past Perfect); this is only used if the original direct speech was already in the past tense.

    • Option D is inconsistent because it changes the first verb but forgets to change "will" and the pronoun "we".

Jobseekers are not

P. being unemployed are a test of faith

Q. self-purification, where the difficulties of

R. relentlessly to a pilgrimage of

S. fatalistic but reapply themselves
spmock003.explanation:
The correct order is SRQP.

spmock003.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form.

We will have made the journey to Wales in five hours.
options: We have made the journey to Wales in five hours.
We make the journey to Wales in five hours.
We will make the journey to Wales in five hours.
We made the journey to Wales in five hours.
spmock003.explanation:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form is (d). Option (d) changes the verb phrase "will have made" (future perfect tense) to "made" (simple past tense). The simple past tense is used to describe actions or events that were completed in the past. The simple past tense is formed by using the past form of the main verb (made). Option (a) is in the present perfect tense, which is formed using "have" + past participle of the verb. Option (b) is in the simple present tense, which is formed using the base form of the verb (make).

Option (c) is in the simple future tense, which is formed using "will" + base form of the verb. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

spmock003.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech:

Kanhaiya said to me, "Do you want to sing?"
options: Kanhaiya enquires if I want to sing.
Kanhaiya said that whether I would sing.
Kanhaiya said that I would sing or not.
Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing.
spmock003.explanation:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Simple Present tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Simple Past tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Said to-Asked/enquired

Do-If

Accordingly, the sentence that follows the above rules of Indirect speech is "Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing."

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

spmock003.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Rajan said to me, "I don't want to go into your house right now."
options: Rajan told me that he do not want to go into my house right then.
Rajan told me that he did not want to go into my house right then.
Rajan told me that he had not wanted to go into my house right now.
Rajan requested me that he wanted to go into my house right then.
spmock003.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject + V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

· The verb 'do' (simple present) is changed into 'did' (simple past).

· The possessive determiner 'your' is changed into 'my'.

· 'Right now' is changed into 'right then'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): Rajan told me that he did not want to go into my house right then.

spmock003.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The ancient texts, which have been meticulously preserved by the monks for centuries,
regarded the sun the primary source of all life and energy on the earth
despite the limited astronomical instruments available to the scholars of that era.
No Error
spmock003.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “the sun the” with “the sun as the”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Mandatory Use of "As" with Specific Verbs -

Certain verbs must be followed by the preposition "as" when they are used to define or describe the complement of an object. These verbs include: Regard, Describe, View, Know, Define, Treat, Characterize.

💢 Application to the Given Question - The verb "regarded" belongs to the category of verbs that require "as" to link the object ("the sun") with its description ("the primary source"). Without "as", the sentence becomes grammatically incomplete and structurally weak.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: I have always regarded him as my brother.

Example 2: The biologist described the specimen as a new species of fungi.

Example 3: He defined success as the ability to overcome repeated failures.

NOTE: Conversely, verbs like Name, Elect, Think, Consider, Call, Choose, Make, and Appoint should NOT be followed by "as".

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

The "Consider" Trap: This is the most common confusion in SSC exams. Consider does not take "as" (e.g., "I consider him my mentor" ✅), but Regard must take "as".

The "Known" Rule: If you use "Known", always check for "as" (e.g., "He is known as the father of chemistry").

Memory Hack: Think of "R-D-V" (Regard, Describe, View). These three are the most frequently tested verbs requiring "as" in CGL Mains

I sat motionless in the passenger seat, feeling trapped in my tight seat belt while Mom sang along with her tapes and pointed at everything she spotted on the roadside. "Oh, Mary, please don't be moody, not today. I told Harry all about how polite and intelligent and cheerful you are," she said. Harry was my mother's new boyfriend, her "significant other," she called him. She'd met him at a business meeting when her company bought the company Harry worked for, and since then she'd been driving over the border to Canada every weekend to see him, leaving me at Dad's. Don't get me wrong, I loved staying with Dad, but I missed my Mom-weekends. We used to make popcorn and watch late-night TV, then sleep in and eat cold breakfast cereal together. Now, when she came to pick me up on Sunday afternoons, she always looked glowing and energetic - and much happier than she ever looked after a weekend spent with me. Last Monday she said something about her and Harry getting married, and that this trip might be the time when he pops the question. The only obstacle before him was meeting me. "I'll be sugar and spice and everything nice, I promise," I said sarcastically, staring out at the Canadian countryside. It pretty much resembled the American countryside only . . . it was more Canadian, somehow. Bigger and emptier, just as I imagined Harry; bigger than Dad, with an enormous head with lots of empty space inside.

spmock003.explanation:
The given passage states that "Now, when she came to pick me up on Sunday afternoons...". In the given sentence, the phrasal verb 'pick up' means 'go somewhere to collect someone, typically in one's car.'

Begin: perform or undergo the first part of (an action or activity).

Note:

Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

A. and unparalleled access to a vast array

C. of knowledge, transforming the way

S1 introduces the context of the interconnected world and sets the tone for the paragraph. Part D provides a specific aspect of the interconnected world, focusing on the internet's role in enabling instant communication. Part D is followed by part B because it elaborates on the idea of communication introduced in part D. Also, 'instant' in part D is an adjective and would appropriately be followed by the noun 'communication' in part B. So, DB is a mandatory pair. Part B mentions the global exchange of information, further expanding on the topic. Part B leads to part A as it provides additional information about the global exchange of information, which includes unparalleled access to a wide variety of knowledge. Part A naturally flows into part C as it talks about unparalleled access to knowledge. Part C then discusses how this access to knowledge is transforming the way things work. The sentence concludes with S6, which summarizes the overall impact of the interconnected world on the way we live and interact. Rearranging parts in the order of DBAC forms a coherent sentence. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The final sentence would be: In today's interconnected world, the internet facilitates instant communication, global information exchange, and unparalleled access to a vast array of knowledge, transforming the way we live and interact.

spmock004.explanation:
If there is any Universal Truth or Habitual Truth in Indirect Speech, there is no change in the tense of Direct Speech.

For example:

The teacher said that humans are mortal. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said, "Humans are mortal." (Direct Speech)

spmock004.word:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

Shravan said that the prisoner had slept throughout the journey.
options: Shravan said, "The prisoner sleeps throughout the journey."
Shravan said, "The prisoner had been sleeping throughout the journey."
Shravan says, "The prisoner has slept throughout the journey."
Shravan said, "The prisoner had slept throughout the journey."
spmock004.explanation:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

Tense remains same

Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

Past perfect changes to Simple Past

Case 1: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) tense will be kept intact.

For example:

He said that he had just finished the movie. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I had just finished the movie" (Direct Speech)

Case 2: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

Case 3: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· Inverted commas are added, and 'that' is removed.

The reporting verb 'said' will remain as such in the direct form. Options (a), (b) and (c) are incorrect according to the change in tense. The first case is applicable here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Shravan said, "The prisoner had slept throughout the journey."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

spmock004.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: Only with this specialized diagnostic tool, the technicians can identify
the minute structural defects within the turbine's internal
components before they lead to a catastrophic mechanical failure.
No Error
spmock004.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

Replace “the technicians can” with “can the technicians”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with "Only + Prepositional Phrase / Adverbial"

When a sentence begins with "Only" followed by a prepositional phrase (e.g., Only with..., Only by..., Only in...) or an adverbial clause (e.g., Only when..., Only after...), the main clause must undergo Inversion. The auxiliary verb (can, could, do, does, did, have, has) must be placed before the subject.

If senetence starts with Only + time / Adverb of manner, use inversion.

Eg. :- Only yesterday, Only then, Only after a month,

Only the day before yesterday, Only after a year, Only in this way,

Only by working hard, etc.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Only with this specialized diagnostic tool, the technicians can identify...

In this sentence, the restrictive phrase "Only with this specialized diagnostic tool" is placed at the very beginning to emphasize the condition. According to the rule of inversion, the auxiliary verb "can" must move to the position before the subject "the technicians" to maintain the correct grammatical structure of the sentence.

Corrected Sentence

Only with this specialized diagnostic tool can the technicians identify the minute structural defects within the turbine's internal components before they lead to a catastrophic mechanical failure.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: Only by working hard can you achieve success in the SSC CGL exam.

Example 2 ✅: Only after the storm subsided did we venture outside to check the damage.

Example 3 ✅: Only in this small village can such rare artifacts be found.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • The "Only" Trap: Remember that inversion doesn't happen if "Only" modifies the subject directly (e.g., "Only the technicians can identify the error" is correct and requires no inversion).

  • Identify the Phrase: Look for a preposition (with, by, in) or a conjunction (when, after) immediately following "Only".

  • The Main Clause: In complex sentences starting with Only when or Only after, the inversion happens in the main clause, not the subordinate clause.

spmock005.word:
Renewable energy is often presented as an uncomplicated remedy to the twin crises of climate change and energy insecurity. Governments announce ambitious targets, corporations highlight sustainability commitments, and public discourse treats renewables as an inevitable successor to fossil fuels. Yet this narrative of inevitability conceals a more complex reality. Transitioning to renewable energy is not merely a technological substitution but a structural transformation involving land use, grid stability, economic redistribution, and political negotiation. Ignoring these dimensions risks replacing one form of dependency with another. One persistent challenge lies in intermittency. Solar and wind energy, while abundant, are not continuously available, requiring storage systems or backup infrastructure. Although technological advances have reduced costs, large-scale storage remains economically and logistically constrained. As a result, renewable integration often relies on conventional energy sources during periods of low generation. This dependence complicates claims of energy independence and exposes the limits of viewing renewables as a standalone solution.

Social and environmental trade-offs further complicate the transition. Large renewable projects demand vast land areas, sometimes displacing communities or disrupting local ecosystems. Ironically, projects designed to mitigate environmental harm can generate localized ecological and social resistance. When decision-making excludes affected populations, renewable energy risks replicating the extractive logic historically associated with fossil fuels—only under a different moral banner.

The long-term success of renewable energy, therefore, depends less on technological optimism and more on institutional capacity. Transparent governance, adaptive grid management, and equitable distribution of costs and benefits are critical. Without these, renewable energy may expand in capacity yet fall short in legitimacy, provoking resistance that slows the very transition it seeks to accelerate.

In the sentence
“Ignoring these dimensions risks replacing one form of dependency with another,”
the phrase “replacing one form of dependency with another” functions as:
options: A participial phrase describing “dependency
A relative clause modifying “dimensions”
An adverbial clause indicating cause
A gerund phrase acting as the object of “risks”
spmock005.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - A gerund phrase acting as the object of “risks”.

Explanation:
The verb “risks” is followed by a gerund phrase explaining what is being risked. The entire phrase functions as the object of the verb.

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG:
B is incorrect because the phrase does not modify “dimensions.”
C is wrong as no cause–effect clause structure exists.
A misidentifies the grammatical role of the phrase.

spmock006.explanation:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

"Informed" changes to "said to".

"was getting" changes to "is getting".

Therefore, the correct answer is: "I said to them, "The weather is getting colder.""

Hence, option (d) is correct.

spmock006.explanation:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Present Conditional Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Future Simple Tense.

Present Conditional (Subject + would/should + V1 +object) will be converted into Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object).

For example:

spmock006.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: Although the rescue teams worked tirelessly,
the floodwaters subsided by the time the relief
materials arrived at the temporary camps.
spmock006.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “subsided” with “had subsided”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Sequence of Tenses (Past Perfect vs. Simple Past)

Past perfect + ‘by the time’ + past indefinite

When two actions happen in the past, one after another, the action that happened first must be in the Past Perfect Tense (Subject + had + V3). The action that happened later must be in the Simple Past Tense (Subject + V2).

When using the phrase "By the time," it acts as a deadline. The event that was already completed before this deadline is the "earlier" action and requires the Past Perfect.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...the floodwaters subsided by the time the relief materials arrived..."

In this sentence, two events are being compared:

  1. The floodwaters receded (First action).

  2. The relief materials arrived (Second action/Deadline).

Because the water had already finished receding before the materials reached the camp, "subsided" must be changed to "had subsided" to maintain the correct chronological order of the past.

Corrected Sentence

Although the rescue teams worked tirelessly, the floodwaters had subsided by the time the relief materials arrived at the temporary camps.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: By the time the doctor reached the hospital, the patient had recovered.

Example 2 ✅: The film had already started by the time we entered the cinema hall.

Example 3 ✅: By the time the police raided the hideout, the culprits had escaped.

As expected, these words settled somewhere beyond her reach, so she gave my comment its only sensible response: "Maybe you should turn down the ringer." "Come here, let me explain why I hate phones, and why my father is to blame. He was a troubled man," I said, because that's how it had been said to me. She listened with attentive eyes, but I knew she'd be confused by what I said next: "And he'd play Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera. Over and over." She lowered her head in search of a link and looked up when she found one. "Is that solitaire?" This time I allowed a smile. "Sometimes he'd conduct an invisible orchestra, waving arms in an erratic fashion, and sometimes he'd sit and listen. But Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera, that one commanded a different reaction. From the start, he stood at full attention, motionless until the end. It went like this for a long time, then he left."

"I soon became his replacement. I'd sit in the study and listen to his music. One evening mother said he wanted to talk to me. I asked if I was going to see him and she said that he'd call. I asked if I could use the phone in his study and she said I could." At this point my companion, attentive as ever, offered her second assumption of the evening, and though more likely than the first, it was just as wrong: "And he never called and that's why you hate phones." No, that's not why. "When mother told me he was on the line, I rushed to the study and dropped the needle on Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera, then picked up the phone. With her final assumption, she came closer to the truth: "So phones remind you of your father, and that's why you hate them."

"That's part of it," I said, "but there's more. He said he could hear Vivaldi in the background and told me to keep listening, that aria was on to something. Then he said goodbye to me and mother and everyone else. Forever. He found his peace." The music prevented a silence that would've felt more comfortable, then it finally stopped and I let the silence prevail. Nature, through millions of years of evolution, has perfected designs that are energy-efficient, sustainable, and highly adaptable. Engineers are increasingly looking to the natural world to develop innovative solutions to complex problems, whether in architecture, manufacturing, or materials science.

By mimicking the hook-and-loop mechanism of the burrs, Mestral created a fastening system that is now widely used. Biomimicry offers more than just clever designs. It emphasizes the importance of sustainability. In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

Rutu said to her brother, "If I were you, I would always come here while the sun was setting."
options: Rutu told her brother that if she was him, she would always go there while the sun was setting.
Rutu advised her brother that if she was him, she would always go there while the sun had been setting.
Rutu told her brother that if she had been him, she would have always gone there while the sun was setting.
Rutu advised her brother that if she were him, she would always go there while the sun was setting.
spmock007.explanation:
The correct answer is Option D: Rutu advised her brother that if she were him, she would always go there while the sun was setting.

Key Points:

  • The "Advice" Verb: Since "If I were you" is a standard way of offering a suggestion, the reporting verb "advised" is more contextually accurate than "said" or "told."

  • The Subjunctive "Were": In hypothetical conditions ("If I were..."), the word "were" is preserved in indirect speech. It does not change to "was" or "had been".

  • The Simultaneous Action Exception: This is the biggest trap. Rules for past habits or actions happening at the same time (connected by "while") dictate that the tense does not change. Therefore, "was setting" stays exactly as "was setting".

  • The Place Shift: The word "here" must change to "there" to reflect the change in perspective.

Breaking Down the Incorrect Options:

  • Option A: Incorrectly changes the subjunctive "were" to "was" and uses the weaker reporting verb "told."

  • Option B: falls for the common trap of shifting a simultaneous action into the past perfect ("had been setting"), which is grammatically incorrect for parallel past events.

  • Option C: Incorrectly treats the hypothetical scenario as a completed past fact by using "had been... would have gone."

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, when converting direct speech into indirect speech, the present modal verbs (can/may/must/will/shall) should be changed into past modal verbs (could/might/had to/would/should).

Example: She said, "I can speak ten languages." (Direct Speech)

She said that she could speak ten languages. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to me' is changed to 'asked me'.

'If' is introduced in the sentence.

'Can you' will be changed to 'I could'

'Help me' will be changed to 'Help him'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.

The Correct Ans is Option D

👉 No Error.

📌 Rule / Concept: Subjunctive Mood with "As though" / "As if"

The conjunctions "as though" and "as if" are used to describe a hypothetical or imaginary situation. The tense used in the following clause depends on the relationship between the two actions:

Past Tense (Unreal Present): Used to describe a situation that is contrary to the present fact (e.g., He talks as though he were a king).

Past Perfect Tense (Unreal Past): Used when the hypothetical situation refers to a time prior to the action in the main clause. If the main verb is in the past tense (explained), the past perfect (had known) correctly indicates a hypothetical prior state.

Corrected Sentence: The officer explained the situation as though he had prior knowledge of every development in the case. (No correction required)

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: He behaves as if he owned the whole company. (Unreal present/general state)

Example 2: She looked as though she had seen a ghost. (Unreal past relative to the looking)

spmock013.word:
Renewable energy is often presented as an uncomplicated remedy to the twin crises of climate change and energy insecurity. Governments announce ambitious targets, corporations highlight sustainability commitments, and public discourse treats renewables as an inevitable successor to fossil fuels. Yet this narrative of inevitability conceals a more complex reality. Transitioning to renewable energy is not merely a technological substitution but a structural transformation involving land use, grid stability, economic redistribution, and political negotiation. Ignoring these dimensions risks replacing one form of dependency with another. One persistent challenge lies in intermittency. Solar and wind energy, while abundant, are not continuously available, requiring storage systems or backup infrastructure. Although technological advances have reduced costs, large-scale storage remains economically and logistically constrained. As a result, renewable integration often relies on conventional energy sources during periods of low generation. This dependence complicates claims of energy independence and exposes the limits of viewing renewables as a standalone solution.

Social and environmental trade-offs further complicate the transition. Large renewable projects demand vast land areas, sometimes displacing communities or disrupting local ecosystems. Ironically, projects designed to mitigate environmental harm can generate localized ecological and social resistance. When decision-making excludes affected populations, renewable energy risks replicating the extractive logic historically associated with fossil fuels—only under a different moral banner.

The long-term success of renewable energy, therefore, depends less on technological optimism and more on institutional capacity. Transparent governance, adaptive grid management, and equitable distribution of costs and benefits are critical. Without these, renewable energy may expand in capacity yet fall short in legitimacy, provoking resistance that slows the very transition it seeks to accelerate.

The word “intermittency” as used in the passage most nearly means:
options: Gradual decline in energy output
Irregular and inconsistent availability
Intentional limitation of energy supply
Temporary surplus of power generation
spmock013.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - Irregular and inconsistent availability.

Explanation:
In context, intermittency refers to the fact that solar and wind energy are not continuously available and depend on natural conditions, creating variability in supply.

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG:
A implies long-term reduction, which is not intended.
C suggests deliberate restriction, which is inaccurate.
D reverses the meaning by implying excess rather than inconsistency.

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. Renewable energy is often presented as an uncomplicated remedy to the twin crises of climate change and energy insecurity. Governments announce ambitious targets, corporations highlight sustainability commitments, and public discourse treats renewables as an inevitable successor to fossil fuels. Yet this narrative of inevitability conceals a more complex reality. Transitioning to renewable energy is not merely a technological substitution but a structural transformation involving land use, grid stability, economic redistribution, and political negotiation. Ignoring these dimensions risks replacing one form of dependency with another. One persistent challenge lies in intermittency. Solar and wind energy, while abundant, are not continuously available, requiring storage systems or backup infrastructure. Although technological advances have reduced costs, large-scale storage remains economically and logistically constrained. As a result, renewable integration often relies on conventional energy sources during periods of low generation. This dependence complicates claims of energy independence and exposes the limits of viewing renewables as a standalone solution.

Social and environmental trade-offs further complicate the transition. Large renewable projects demand vast land areas, sometimes displacing communities or disrupting local ecosystems. Ironically, projects designed to mitigate environmental harm can generate localized ecological and social resistance. When decision-making excludes affected populations, renewable energy risks replicating the extractive logic historically associated with fossil fuels—only under a different moral banner.

The long-term success of renewable energy, therefore, depends less on technological optimism and more on institutional capacity. Transparent governance, adaptive grid management, and equitable distribution of costs and benefits are critical. Without these, renewable energy may expand in capacity yet fall short in legitimacy, provoking resistance that slows the very transition it seeks to accelerate.

The tone of the passage is best described as:
options: Cautiously critical of oversimplified narratives around renewable energy
Enthusiastic and optimistic about technological breakthroughs
Dismissive of renewable energy as an impractical alternative
Neutral and purely informational about energy systems
spmock014.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - Cautiously critical of oversimplified narratives around renewable energy.

Explanation:
The passage acknowledges the importance of renewable energy but consistently critiques the assumption that it is a simple or inevitable solution. The tone balances recognition with caution, emphasizing structural and social complexities.

Note:

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

The original sentence contains an error due to the use of the phrase "put down." The expression "put down" typically means to physically place something on a surface or to euthanize an animal, but it does not convey the intended meaning of postponing or cancelling an event, such as a match in this context.

Option (a) is correct. The phrasal verb "put off" means to postpone or delay something to a later time. In the context of the sentence, it accurately conveys the idea that the team captain had to postpone or reschedule the match due to the sudden unavailability of several key players.

Option (b) is not correct. This phrasal verb "put on" commonly means to dress oneself by placing clothing, accessories, or items onto one's body. However, in the context of the sentence, it doesn't convey the idea of postponement or cancellation of the match due to the unavailability of players.

Option (c) is incorrect. The phrase 'call back' usually means to return a phone call or ask someone to return to a place or situation. However, it doesn't accurately convey the action needed in the given context, where the team captain must take a decision regarding the match due to the absence of key players.

Option (d) is incorrect as well. "Call on" often means to ask for assistance or support from someone. However, in the context of the sentence, it doesn't convey the team captain's action of postponing or cancelling the match due to the sudden unavailability of players.

The correct sentence is: The team captain had to put off the match due to the sudden unavailability of several key players.

NOTE:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb 'being' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

spmock018.explanation:
Imperative Sentences sometimes begin with Negative Commands like "Don't"

"Forbade" is sometimes used while transforming Direct Speech into Indirect Speech.

For example:

My friend said to me, "Don't read this novel". (Direct Speech)

· The verb 'Do not smoke' is changed into the infinitive 'to smoke'.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Once upon a time, in a grand estate perched on a hill, there lived an arrogant woman named Victoria. Victoria had recently married a wealthy widower, becoming the stepmother to his young son, Thomas. Her arrival brought an air of entitlement and superiority that cast a shadow over their once happy home. Victoria saw Thomas as an obstacle to her new life of luxury. She resented his presence, considering him an inconvenience that stood in the way of her ambitions. Thomas, despite his tender age, possessed a resilient spirit. He yearned for his father's love and acceptance, but Victoria's coldness only incited his determination to rise above her contemptuous behaviour. He sought solace in his own imagination, finding refuge in books and daydreams that transported him far away from the reality of their toxic household.

Victoria's arrogance began to crumble as she witnessed the positive impact Thomas had on others. She saw his unwavering kindness and the light he brought into their home. Slowly, her heart softened, and she realized the error of her ways. Regret filled her as she reflected on the years of mistreatment and the missed opportunities to build a genuine bond with Thomas. In a moment of vulnerability, Victoria approached Thomas, seeking forgiveness for her past actions. With tears in her eyes, she expressed her remorse and acknowledged the hurt she had caused. Thomas, in a display of grace beyond his years, embraced her with forgiveness, understanding that everyone deserves a chance to change.

From that day forward, Victoria and Thomas worked to rebuild their relationship. Their story became a testament to the transformative power of humility and forgiveness. Victoria learned that true strength lies not in arrogance, but in the ability to acknowledge one's mistakes and grow from them. And Thomas, through his resilience and capacity for forgiveness, showed that love can prevail, even in the face of adversity. In the end, their journey together taught them both valuable lessons about the importance of compassion, empathy, and the capacity for change.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The power of imagination and escapism in challenging circumstances.
The importance of wealth and luxury in finding happiness.
The struggles of a blended family and the impact of a stepmother's arrogance.
The transformative power of forgiveness and humility in rebuilding relationships.
spmock018.explanation:
The main idea of the passage is the transformative power of forgiveness and humility in rebuilding relationships. Throughout the passage, we see the initial conflict between Victoria, the arrogant stepmother, and Thomas, the young stepson. Victoria's arrogance and mistreatment of Thomas created a toxic environment in their home. However, as the story progresses, Victoria begins to witness Thomas's unwavering kindness and the positive impact he has on others. This leads to a change of heart in Victoria, and she realizes the error of her ways. In a vulnerable moment, she approaches Thomas, seeking forgiveness for her past actions.

spmock018.word:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

The introduction of African cheetahs to India was planned without considering their spatial ecology, according to researchers who warn that the released animals may come into conflict with people in the neighbouring villages. Spatial ecology addresses the fundamental effects of space on the movement of individual species and on the stability of multispecies communities. A total of 20 cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa were introduced to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh last year to establish a free-ranging population - for the first time since their extinction in India 70 years ago. Scientists of the Cheetah Research Project of Leibniz-IZW in Namibia argue that in southern Africa, cheetahs live in a stable socio-spatial system with widely spread territories and densities of less than one individual per 100 square kilometres (km²). The plan for cheetahs in Kuno National Park assumes that the high prey density will sustain high cheetah densities, even though there is no evidence for that, they said. In a letter published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice on Thursday, researchers noted that as Kuno National Park is small, it is likely that the released animals will move far beyond the park's boundaries and cause conflicts with neighbouring villages.

According to a calculation of the local prey density, it was calculated that 21 adult cheetahs could be sustained by the prey base in Kuno National Park - equivalent to a density of about three individuals per 100 km². Based on their research results from a long-term study of the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in Namibia, as well as comparable work in East Africa, scientists from the Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Leibniz-IZW warn against overestimating the carrying capacity of the area. The carrying capacity is usually between 0.2 and 1 adult per 100 km² for cheetahs under natural conditions. This is true not only for Namibia but also for the ecologically very different conditions in the Serengeti ecosystem in East Africa which has a much higher density of prey, they said. The team formulated predictions about the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in their new habitat, identifying controversial issues and hidden core assumptions of the reintroduction plan. These assumptions ignore important aspects of the cheetah socio-spatial system.

Read the statements given below.

A. The carrying capacity of 3 cheetahs per 100 km square is currently feasible in Kuno National Park.

B. The carrying capacity for cheetahs is different in Kuno national park when compared to carrying capacity of parks in Africa.
options: Both A and B are true but B is not the correct reason for A.
Both A and B are true and B is the correct reason for A.
A is false and B is true.
A is true and B is false.
spmock018.explanation:
Statement A is false. The first sentence of the second paragraph states that "According to a calculation of the local prey density, it was calculated that 21 adult cheetahs could be sustained by the prey base in Kuno National Park - equivalent to a density of about three individuals per 100 km²." According to this, the carrying capacity for Kuno National Park is 3 cheetahs per 100 km². The second paragraph also states that "The carrying capacity is usually between 0.2 and 1 adult per 100 km² for cheetahs under natural conditions." So, as per the passage, the current carrying capacity may not be feasible.

Statement B is true. The last sentence of the first paragraph suggests that Kuno National Park is small, and cheetahs might move far beyond the park's boundaries and cause conflicts with neighbouring villages. So, the carrying capacity of Kuno National Park is not the same as in Africa. The third and fourth sentences in the second paragraph corroborate this.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Sentence D provides further context by citing specific research findings. spmock019.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The Aryans utilized swift horses in
their military campaigns that was the
primary reason for their tactical superiority.
No Error
spmock019.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

Replace “that” with “which”.

Rule / Concept: Relative Pronouns Referring to a Clause -

In English grammar, when we want a relative pronoun to refer back to an entire preceding idea or a whole clause (rather than just the noun immediately before it), we must use "which." The relative pronoun "that" cannot be used to refer to a whole sentence or statement; it can only refer to a specific noun or pronoun (the antecedent).

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, what was the primary reason for their superiority? It wasn't just the "campaigns" (plural) themselves. It was the entire fact/action mentioned in the first part of the sentence: "The Aryans utilized swift horses in their military campaigns." Since the relative pronoun is referring to this entire statement as a single reason, "that" is incorrect. It must be replaced with "which."

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: He passed the exam with flying colors, which surprised everyone. (The fact that he passed surprised them).

Example 2 ✅: It rained all day, which ruined our plans for the picnic. (The fact that it rained ruined the plans).

Example 3 ✅: She ignored my advice, which was a very foolish thing to do. (The act of ignoring advice was foolish).

spmock019.word:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I told Pooja that she could have use my car to get around while she is in my hometown.
options: that she could have use my car to get around with
that she can use my car to get around
that she could have use my car to get away
that she can use my car to get away with
spmock019.explanation:
The usage of the word 'use' is incorrect in the underlined part. Either the third form of a verb should be used after the helping verb 'have', or the word 'have' should be removed from the sentence so that the first form of the verb fits appropriately after the modal verb 'could/can' in the sentence. So, options (a) and (c) are incorrect as they do not rectify this error.

Option (d) is incorrect as 'to get away with' means 'to escape'. It does not make the sentence coherent as one cannot escape a place and yet stay in the speaker's hometown.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Note: Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as the possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

spmock019.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Jake thought no one knew how much he liked Julie, but his face when he got to know that she'll be at the party really _______!

Among these options, only 'gave him away' is grammatically correct and at the same time, results in a meaningful sentence/idea - 'his secret feelings for Julie were evident on his face when Jake got to know that she'll be there'.

The answer is option (b).

Note:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - She likes cooking. [singular subject and verb] -- They like to cook vegetables. [plural subject and verb]

spmock019.word:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

The introduction of African cheetahs to India was planned without considering their spatial ecology, according to researchers who warn that the released animals may come into conflict with people in the neighbouring villages. Spatial ecology addresses the fundamental effects of space on the movement of individual species and on the stability of multispecies communities. A total of 20 cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa were introduced to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh last year to establish a free-ranging population - for the first time since their extinction in India 70 years ago. Scientists of the Cheetah Research Project of Leibniz-IZW in Namibia argue that in southern Africa, cheetahs live in a stable socio-spatial system with widely spread territories and densities of less than one individual per 100 square kilometres (km²). The plan for cheetahs in Kuno National Park assumes that the high prey density will sustain high cheetah densities, even though there is no evidence for that, they said. In a letter published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice on Thursday, researchers noted that as Kuno National Park is small, it is likely that the released animals will move far beyond the park's boundaries and cause conflicts with neighbouring villages.

According to a calculation of the local prey density, it was calculated that 21 adult cheetahs could be sustained by the prey base in Kuno National Park - equivalent to a density of about three individuals per 100 km². Based on their research results from a long-term study of the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in Namibia, as well as comparable work in East Africa, scientists from the Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Leibniz-IZW warn against overestimating the carrying capacity of the area. The carrying capacity is usually between 0.2 and 1 adult per 100 km² for cheetahs under natural conditions. This is true not only for Namibia but also for the ecologically very different conditions in the Serengeti ecosystem in East Africa which has a much higher density of prey, they said. The team formulated predictions about the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in their new habitat, identifying controversial issues and hidden core assumptions of the reintroduction plan. These assumptions ignore important aspects of the cheetah socio-spatial system.

Why did the authorities think Cheetahs could sustain themselves in the small boundaries of Kuno National Park?
options: The meagreness of the prey could help the sustainability of cheetahs.
The availability of prey could sustain more cheetahs in a limited space.
High number of cheetahs could control the number of prey.
A large number of prey and food sources can only be reduced with a high number of cheetahs.
spmock019.explanation:
The first paragraph states that "The plan for cheetahs in Kuno National Park assumes that the high prey density will sustain high cheetah densities, even though there is no evidence for that, they said." According to this, the authorities thought that a large number of prey could help sustain a high density of cheetahs.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

spmock019.word:
Renewable energy is often presented as an uncomplicated remedy to the twin crises of climate change and energy insecurity. Governments announce ambitious targets, corporations highlight sustainability commitments, and public discourse treats renewables as an inevitable successor to fossil fuels. Yet this narrative of inevitability conceals a more complex reality. Transitioning to renewable energy is not merely a technological substitution but a structural transformation involving land use, grid stability, economic redistribution, and political negotiation. Ignoring these dimensions risks replacing one form of dependency with another. One persistent challenge lies in intermittency. Solar and wind energy, while abundant, are not continuously available, requiring storage systems or backup infrastructure. Although technological advances have reduced costs, large-scale storage remains economically and logistically constrained. As a result, renewable integration often relies on conventional energy sources during periods of low generation. This dependence complicates claims of energy independence and exposes the limits of viewing renewables as a standalone solution.

Social and environmental trade-offs further complicate the transition. Large renewable projects demand vast land areas, sometimes displacing communities or disrupting local ecosystems. Ironically, projects designed to mitigate environmental harm can generate localized ecological and social resistance. When decision-making excludes affected populations, renewable energy risks replicating the extractive logic historically associated with fossil fuels—only under a different moral banner.

The long-term success of renewable energy, therefore, depends less on technological optimism and more on institutional capacity. Transparent governance, adaptive grid management, and equitable distribution of costs and benefits are critical. Without these, renewable energy may expand in capacity yet fall short in legitimacy, provoking resistance that slows the very transition it seeks to accelerate.

Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the passage?
options: Renewable Energy and the Future of Climate Policy
Technological Barriers to Sustainable Power
Beyond the Promise: The Complex Reality of Renewable Energy
Why Energy Storage Determines Global Sustainability
spmock019.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - Beyond the Promise: The Complex Reality of Renewable Energy.

Explanation:
This title captures the passage’s central argument that renewable energy is often portrayed too simply, while its actual implementation involves political, social, and infrastructural challenges.

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG:
A is too broad and policy-focused, missing the structural critique.
B narrows the issue to technology, ignoring social and institutional factors.
D overemphasizes storage, which is only one part of the argument.
