spmock019.word:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The car was repaired by the mechanic.
options: The mechanic has repaired the car.
The mechanic is repairing the car.
spmock019.explanation:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (4) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

spmock019.word:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

After we come to power at the Centre, we will conduct a countrywide caste census.
options: A countrywide caste census should be conducted by us when we come to power at the Centre.
A countrywide caste census will have been conducted by us after we come to power at the Centre.
A countrywide caste census will be conducted by us as and when we come to power at the Centre.
A countrywide caste census will be conducted by us after we come to power at the Centre.
spmock019.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb ['have been' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive. In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Mohan asked,' Do you live in the hostel, Zoya?'

Mohan asked if Zoya lives in the hostel.
Mohan asked me whether Zoya lived in the hostel.

The question is directed to Zoya, not to the reader ('me'), and neither is it a general question. Hence options (a) and (d) are eliminated.

The verb must be changed from simple present to simple past. ('live' to 'lived'), as the reported verb ('asked') is in past tense.

When the question doesn't start with a 'wh-' word, the reporting verb is followed by an 'if' or 'whether'.

Hence, the correct sentence in indirect speech is: Mohan asked Zoya whether she lived in the hostel.

Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

spmock019.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The man said that he did not see any chance of success except by bribery.

The man said, "I don't see any chance of success except by bribery."
spmock019.explanation:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Simple Past Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Simple Present Tense.

Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object) will be converted into Simple Present (Subject +V1st + Object).

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· The verb 'did not see' (simple past) is changed into 'do not see' (simple present).

· The pronoun 'he' is changed into 'I'.

All options except (d) don't follow the grammatical structure. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The man said, "I don't see any chance of success except by bribery."

spmock019.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

and revolution that are responsible for the earth gravitational
changes affecting the climate throughout the year.
No Error
spmock019.explanation:

Replace “earth” with “earth's”

Rule / Concept: Possessive Case of Celestial Bodies

While we generally avoid using the apostrophe 's with inanimate objects (e.g., we say "the legs of the table," not "the table's legs"), certain nouns are treated as exceptions due to their dignity, personification, or astronomical significance.

Nouns representing celestial bodies—such as the Earth, Sun, Moon, and Planets—are traditionally used with the possessive 's when referring to their properties, movements, or influences.

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, "gravitational changes" belong to the "Earth." Since Earth is a celestial body, it requires the possessive form to show this relationship. Leaving it as "earth" makes it a noun adjunct that sounds incomplete or ungrammatical in formal writing. Adding the apostrophe and 's' correctly identifies the gravity as a property belonging to our planet.

Option (c) uses the phrase "gaze at the torn," which lacks the past tense required to match the context of the sentence. The sentence discusses a past event, and "gaze" in the simple present tense doesn't align with the past tense narrative required in this context.

Option (a) uses the present participle "looking," which does not align with the past tense context of the sentence.

Option (d) is incorrect as 'were' needs to be followed by either past participle (v3 form) or present participle (-ing form of verb), but 'gaze' is a base verb.

The correct sentence is: He couldn't help but feel a pang of regret as he gazed at the faded photograph, a visual reminder of the friendships he had let drift away over the years.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

spmock020.word:
Directions :Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

We sit in the last row, bumped about but free of stares. The bus rolls out of the dull cross roads of the city, and we are soon in the open country side, with fields of sunflowers as far as the eye can see, their heads all facing us. Where there is no water, the land reverts to the desert. While still on level ground, we see in the distance the tall range of the Mount Bogda, abrupt like a shining prism laid horizontally on the desert surface. It is over 5,000 metres high, and the peaks are under permanent snow, in powerful contrast to the flat desert all around. Heaven lake lies part of the way up this range, about 2,000 metres above sea level, at the foot of one of the highest snow-peaks.

As the bus climbs, the sky, brilliant before, grows overcast. I have brought nothing warm to wear. It is all down at the hotel in Urumqi. Rain begins to fall. The man behind me is eating over poweringly smelly goat's cheese. The bus window leaks inhospitably but reveals a beautiful view. We have passed quickly from the desert through arable land to pasture and the ground is now green with grass, the slopes dark with pine. A few cattle drink at a clear stream flowing past moss-covered stones; it is a Constable landscape. The stream changes into a white torrent, and as we climb higher. I wish more and more that I had brought with me something warmer than the pair of shorts that have served me so well in the desert. The stream (which, we are told, rises in Heaven Lake) disappears, and we continue our slow ascent. About noon, we arrive at Heaven Lake, and look for a place to stay at the foot, which is the resort area. We get a room in a small cottage, and I am happy to note that there are thick quilts on the bed.

Standing outside the cottage, we survey our surroundings. Heaven Lake is long, sardine-shaped and fed by snowmelt from a stream at its head. The lake is an intense blue, surrounded on all sides by green mountain walls, dotted with distant sheep. At the head of the lake, beyond the delta of the inflowing stream, is a massive snow-capped peak which dominates the vista; it is part of a series of peaks that culminate, a little out of view, in Mount Bogda itself.

For those who live in the resort, there is a small mess-hall by the shore. We eat here sometimes, and sometimes buy food from the vendors outside, who sell kabab and naan until the last buses leave. The kababs, cooked on skewers over charcoal braziers, are particularly good; highly spiced and well-done. Horse's milk is available too from the local Kazakh herdsmen, but I decline this. I am so affected by the cold that Mr.Cao, the relaxed young man who runs the mess, lends me a spare pair of trousers, several sizes too large but more than comfortable. Once I am warm again, I feel a pre-dinner spurt of energy - dinner will belong incoming - and I ask him whether the lake is good for swimming in.

Select an appropriate title for the passage.
spmock020.explanation:
The author sees Mount Bogda while on the journey to Lake Heaven. So, 'Journey to Mount Bogda' cannot be an appropriate title.

'Shorts to trousers' is the sub-plot of the story where the author mentions that he only has the pair of shorts and how after reaching the Lake Heaven, Mr. Cao, one who runs the mess, offered him the trousers. So, from options (a) and (b), option (b) is the more appropriate title, as the story is about the author's account of the visit to Lake Heaven.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

'Peasant Life' is completely out of context to be the title of the given passage.

spmock020.word:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Biomimicry, the practice of drawing inspiration from nature to solve human challenges, is revolutionizing modern engineering. Nature, through millions of years of evolution, has perfected designs that are energy-efficient, sustainable, and highly adaptable. Engineers are increasingly looking to the natural world to develop innovative solutions to complex problems, whether in architecture, manufacturing, or materials science.

One of the most famous examples of biomimicry is the development of Velcro. The idea came from Swiss engineer George de Mestral, who observed how burrs stuck to his dog's fur. By mimicking the hook-and-loop mechanism of the burrs, Mestral created a fastening system that is now widely used. Another key example is the design of energy-efficient buildings inspired by termite mounds. Termites construct their nests with natural ventilation systems that maintain a stable temperature, even in extreme heat. Inspired by this, architects have designed climate-responsive buildings that reduce the need for artificial heating or cooling, saving energy.

In materials science, the lotus leaf's ability to resist dirt and water has led to the development of self-cleaning surfaces. These surfaces use microstructures similar to those on the leaf, preventing the accumulation of dust or grime. Similarly, researchers are studying the structure of spider silk, which is both incredibly strong and lightweight, to create synthetic materials for use in everything from medical sutures to aerospace components.

Biomimicry offers more than just clever designs. It emphasizes the importance of sustainability. By mimicking nature's solutions, engineers can create technologies that work in harmony with the environment, reducing waste and conserving resources. As this field continues to grow, it promises a future where human innovation is increasingly aligned with the natural world.

What is a key benefit of biomimicry as highlighted in the passage?
options: It focuses mainly on copying the appearance of natural organisms.
It encourages faster industrial production using synthetic chemicals.
It reduces the cost of manufacturing by using cheaper materials.
It promotes sustainable technologies that work in harmony with the environment.
spmock020.explanation:
The last paragraph emphasizes that biomimicry is not just about clever design but also about sustainability. It notes that by mimicking nature's solutions, engineers can reduce waste and conserve resources, creating technologies that align with the environment.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Option (a) is incorrect because biomimicry focuses on function and efficiency, not just appearance.

Option (b) is not mentioned and contradicts the idea of natural, sustainable methods.

Option (c) is not a key focus of the passage; cost reduction is not discussed as a primary benefit.

If + Past Participle, Past Participle.

Note:

Conditional Clause: A conditional clause is the one that usually starts with if or unless and describes something that is possible or probable. Example: If you're going to college, I could give you a lift. Here, "If you are going to the college" is the conditional clause and "I could give you a lift" is the main clause.

spmock020.word:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The shareholders will elect him a director.
options: He will be elected as director by the shareholders.
The shareholders have elected him a director.
The shareholders elected him a director.
He will be elected a director.
spmock020.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (1) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "He will be elected as director by the shareholders.

spmock020.word:

Admittance was refused to him by the airport security.
options: The airport security is refusing him admittance.
The airport security has refused him admittance.
The airport security had refused him admittance .
The airport security refused him admittance.
spmock020.explanation:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

spmock020.word: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.
options: She suggested a elaborate approach but mine is an easier one.
She suggested an elaborate approach but mine is a easier one.

spmock020.explanation:
Note:

Only the sentence in option (d) has the correct use of indefinite articles. The article 'an' is used before words that start with a vowel or a vowel sounding word. Accordingly, 'elaborate' and 'easier' start with a vowel. So, the use of 'an' is correctly used in option (d).

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

spmock020.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Shikha said, "The heavy rain this week has spoiled all my travel plans."
options: Shikha said that the heavy rain that week had spoiled all her travel plans.
Shikha told me that the heavy rain that week had spoiled all her travel plans.
Shikha said that the heavy rain that week has spoiled all her travel plans.
Shikha said that the heavy rain this week had spoiled all her travel plans.
spmock020.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'This week' would be changed to 'that week'.

'Has spoiled' would be changed to 'had spoiled'.

'My' would be changed to 'her'.

Since there is no object of the verb 'said' in the sentence in direct speech, 'said' would be changed to 'said that' only.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Shikha said that the heavy rain that week had spoiled all her travel plans.

spmock020.word:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Mahesh said to Rita, "Don't play in the sun".
options: Mahesh advised Rita not to play in the sun
Mahesh told to Rita to not play in the sun
Mahesh ordered Rita that not play in the sun
Mahesh requested Rita that don't play in the sun
spmock020.explanation:
Imperative Sentences sometimes begin with Negative Commands like "Don't".

The reporting verbs like "said/say", etc. are changed into "asked/ask", "told/tell", "advised/ advise" etc.

"Not + To + V1" is used in these sentences. For example, "don't go" should be changed to "not to go" in Indirect speech.

In this context, "Don't ......" changes into "not to ......".

For example:

My friend said to me, "Don't go to Kolkata." (Direct Speech)

My friend advised me not to go to Kolkata. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to' will be changed to 'advised'.

'Don't play' will be changed to 'not to play'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Mahesh advised Rita not to play in the sun.

spmock020.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The marketing director failed to provide a convincing
cause for the sharp decline in quarterly sales, despite
having access to extensive consumer feedback data.
No Error
spmock020.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “cause” with “reason

Rule / Concept: Reason vs. Cause

1.Cause (Noun): Refers to the person, thing, or event that makes something happen (the origin/producer of an effect).

2.Preposition: Usually followed by "of".

3.Context: Used for physical or scientific results (e.g., the cause of the fire).

4.Reason (Noun): Refers to the justification, explanation, or motive for an action or belief.

5.Preposition: Usually followed by "for".

6.Context: Used for human logic, decisions, or excuses (e.g., the reason for his absence).

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the director is expected to provide an explanation or a justification for the sales performance to the board. This involves human analysis and logic rather than a direct physical trigger. Furthermore, the sentence uses the preposition "for". Since "cause" typically pairs with "of" to indicate a physical origin, and "reason" pairs with "for" to indicate an explanation, "reason" is the correct fit here.

More Examples for Clarity -

1. Scientists are studying the cause of the disease. (Physical origin)

2. There is no reason for you to be angry. (Justification)

3. The reason why he left is unknown.

spmock021.word:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Theories of relativity and quantum mechanics have led physicists to question the linear progression of time, proposing alternative models where time is relative and context-dependent.

B. While time is often measured in seconds, minutes, and hours, its true nature remains a subject of philosophical and scientific inquiry.

C. The human experience of time, influenced by emotions, memories, and perception, continues to fascinate philosophers, psychologists, and scholars seeking to understand its subjective and often paradoxical nature.

D. Time is a constant yet elusive force that shapes human existence, determining the pace of our lives and the course of history.
spmock021.explanation:
The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is DBAC.

Sentence D comes first as it introduces time as an important and constant force that affects human existence. It sets the stage for discussing the broader concept of time.

Sentence B builds on D by acknowledging that although we commonly measure time in units (seconds, minutes, hours), the true nature of time remains a mystery.

Sentence A builds upon B and introduces scientific theories, particularly relativity and quantum mechanics, that challenge conventional views about time. It presents the notion that time might not be linear and may change based on context, thereby deepening the complexity introduced in B.

Sentence C shifts to the subjective experience of time (as opposed to the physical and scientific aspects discussed earlier). It highlights the fascination with time from a human perspective, connecting the scientific views in A to the emotional and psychological experience of time. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

spmock021.word:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. As cost of raw materials cannot be reduced, exporters try to cut labour costs.

B. Large MNCs in the garment industry in Europe and America order their products from Indian exporters.

C. These large MNCs with worldwide network look for the cheapest goods in order to maximise their profits.

D. To get these large orders, Indian garment exporters try hard to cut their own costs.

spmock021.explanation:
The paragraph discusses Indian garment exporters' cost-cutting for MNC orders. Sentence B introduces MNCs ordering from Indian exporters, setting the context. Sentence C explains why MNCs seek cheap goods (to maximize profits), following B. Sentence D describes Indian exporters' efforts to cut costs to secure orders, linking to C. Sentence A specifies that raw material costs are fixed, so labour costs are targeted, following D. Sentence E elaborates on how labour costs are cut (temporary workers), concluding the sequence.

The order B-C-D-A-E forms a coherent paragraph.

Option B is correct.

spmock021.word:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A) They decided to starts a small business together. They have already secured a location and are preparing for their grand opening.

B) They decided to started a small business together. They have already secured a location and are preparing for their grand opening.

C) They decided to started a small business together. They have already secured a location and are preparing for there grand opening.

D) They decided to start a small business together. They have already secured a location and are preparing for their grand opening.
spmock021.explanation:
The grammatically correct sentence is D. After the infinitive marker "to", we usually use the base form of the verb. So, the correct base form to use after 'to' is 'start' (used in D). 'Starts' (used in A) is the present tense form, not the base form of the verb. 'Started' (used in B and C) is the past tense form, not the base form of the verb. Also, in sentence C, "there" should be replaced with "their." "There" is used to refer to a place, while "their" is the possessive form that is needed to indicate that the grand opening belongs to "them." Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

"Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb."

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

spmock021.word:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

In China, there once lived a father, his four sons, and three daughters-in-law. His three older sons had married within a few months of each other and all with young women from the same village. Recently, these three new daughters-in-law had been brought into the house. Their new father-in-law's wife had died a few years before and having no mother-in-law with them in their new home, and being lonesome and homesick for their former families, they constantly asked the old man for permission to visit their former village. For you see, those were the days when young women, after they married and moved into the homes of their new husbands, needed permission to leave the household. Annoyed by the continual pleas of his three new daughters-in-law, the old father thought of a way to put an end to it.

He gave the young women permission in this way, saying, "You are always begging me to allow you to go and visit your mothers, and you think I am very hard-hearted for not letting you go. Now you may go, but only upon this condition. When you come back, you must each bring me something that I want. One of you must bring me some fire in paper, the other must bring me some wind in paper, and the third must bring me some music in wind. Unless you promise to bring me this, you are never to ask me to let you go home. And if you go and fail to get these for me, you are never to come back." The old man did not suppose that these conditions would be accepted. Of course, they were hard to understand, much less to fulfil. But the girls were young and thoughtless, and in their anxiety to get away did not consider any of that. So, they promised and made ready with speed. In great glee, they started off on foot to visit their mothers.

What did the old man ask for in return after permitting his daughters-in-law to visit their respective parents?
options: The old man asked for nothing in return.
He asked for a sack full of gold coins.
He asked that they bring a lot of sweets from home.
He wanted the fulfilment of his three wishes.
spmock021.explanation: The following sentences from the second paragraph of the given passage state "When you come back, you must each bring me something that I want. One of you must bring me some fire in paper, the other must bring me some wind in paper, and the third must bring me some music in wind." Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

spmock021.word:
Directions : Read the given passage and answer the question that follows.

As a result of increasing population and expansion of residential areas, forest lands are being encroached. This is not all; even the wildlife is under extreme threat. As our fauna is facing a dearth of adequate shelter in forests, they are heading towards towns and hence get killed by hunters. Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction. The Black Buck is almost endangered and found only in two countries, Nepal and India. In India, this antelope is found in many national parks like Guindy National Park, Point Calimere and Vellandu sanctuaries of Tamil Nadu, Rollapadu of Andra Pradesh, few parts of Rajasthan and Haryana. As far as their habitat is concerned, they live in open grasslands, dry areas or thinly populated areas and near water resources. They live in the desert areas of Rajasthan and coastal areas because they cannot sustain cold climate. They are the fastest running animals on this planet. Further, this animal is active during the day but slows down in its activities after midday. They are social beings. Hence, they move with their herds, which can vary from 3 to 23 mates. Key Points

  • In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said to" in Direct Speech is changed into "wanted to know", "enquired (of)", or "asked".

  • In Indirect Speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech. This means the question form ("why did you fail") changes to the assertive form ("why they had failed").

  • For "Wh-" questions, the question word (Why, How, etc.) acts as the conjunction itself. Using an additional conjunction like "that" (as seen in the second option) is grammatically incorrect.

  • Tense Change: The sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Past Simple tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Past Perfect tense ("had failed").

  • Time Expression: The word "last week" in Direct Speech changes to "the previous week" in Indirect Speech.

  • Pronoun Change: The second-person pronoun "you" changes according to the object of the reporting verb ("the staff"), becoming "they".

spmock021.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: Despite several rounds of intense deliberations with the international trade
commission, the federal government has still to announce the
comprehensive new tax regulations for the upcoming fiscal year.
No Error
spmock021.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “has still to announce” with “has yet to announce”.

Rule / Concept: Still vs. Yet

  • Still: Used for an action that is continuing (It began in the past and is happening now). It usually goes before the main verb or after the "be" verb.

  • Yet: Used for an action that is expected to happen but hasn't happened. It usually goes at the end of a sentence.

Application to the Given Question

"...the federal government has still to announce the comprehensive new tax regulations..."

In this sentence, the structure used is Subject + Has + [Adverb] + Infinitive (to announce). This specific setup describes a pending action. Grammatically, "still" is incorrect here because "still" describes continuity, whereas "yet" describes something that remains undone. The fixed idiomatic expression for a pending official action is always "has yet to".

Corrected Sentence

Despite several rounds of intense deliberations with the international trade commission, the federal government has yet to announce the comprehensive new tax regulations for the upcoming fiscal year.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: The results have yet to be declared. ✅

Example 2: He is still waiting for the bus. (Continuity) ✅

Example 3: I haven't received the mail yet. (Expected action at the end) ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1: We have still to decide the winner. (Should be have yet to) ✅

Wrong example 2: Is it yet raining outside? (Should be still raining) ✅

spmock022.explanation:
The correct order is ACBEDF.

The sentence begins with the possessive phrase "The athlete's", indicating that something belongs to the athlete. It is to be followed by the noun phrase "incredible performance", describing what the athlete did. The phrase "shattered records" describes the result or consequence of the performance, indicating that existing records were broken. The conjunction "and" connects the two parts of the sentence. The phrase "established a new benchmark" describes another result of the performance, indicating that a new standard was set. Lastly, the prepositional phrase "in their respective sport" specifies the specific domain or field in which the records were shattered, and the benchmark was established. By arranging these parts in the given order, the sentence forms a coherent and meaningful statement.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The rearranged sentence is: The athlete's incredible performance shattered records and established a new benchmark in their respective sport.

Note:

Prepositional phrase: A modifying phrase consisting of a preposition and its object. Example: The cat was hiding under the table. Here, 'under' is the preposition while 'table' is its object.

Possessive nouns are types of nouns that show ownership or connection. All nouns become possessive nouns with the addition of an apostrophe and a suffix - the letter "s" - at the end of the word. However, when a plural noun ends in the letter "s," the possessive form of the word only requires the use of an apostrophe at the end. Possessive nouns can be tricky because they function like adjectives by modifying another noun or pronoun in the sentence. E.g., "Timmy's dog is cute."

Noun phrase: A noun phrase is built around a single noun. Example: Their website published an article about the importance of focused work. Here 'article' is a noun and the part highlighted is a noun phrase.

spmock023.word:

options: Tall promises were being made by each candidate.

spmock023.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

The options except (1) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

spmock023.word: Describe how you will say What is Tina carrying in her bag? in passive voice.
options: When is being carried by Tina in her bag?

spmock023.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb 'being' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

Case 1: "Which/What" etc are placed as they are.

For example:

Case 2: When "Which/What" is used as a subject in Active voice, it is changed into "By what" in Passive voice.

For example:

By what are you being made happy? (Passive)

Also, the sentence is in the Present continuous tense in the Active voice. So, in the Passive voice, Present continuous tense should be used.

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below: Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground. Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion. The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect. The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. spmock023.word:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Identify the options that arrange the part in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. It took two days

B. who had set out

C. spotted by one of his

D. for him to be

E. fellow fishermen

F. to search for him
spmock023.explanation:
In all the options, A is the first part, and F is the last part. Only phrase D can follow A. The preposition 'for' connects the purpose of those two days. 'To be' is followed by a participle verb. Therefore, only C can follow D because 'spotted' here will be the past participle. 'His' is a possessive determiner which requires a noun after it. So, the phrase 'fellow fisherman' can follow C. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the subject of the sentence/clause (living things). So, B follows E. The correct order is ADCEBF.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: It took two days for him to be spotted by one of his fellow fishermen who had set out to search for him.

Note:

"Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective."

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

He will have read the book that we sent him yesterday.
options: The book that we sent him yesterday would have been read by him.
The book that we had sent him yesterday would have been read by him.
The book that we sent him yesterday will have been read by him.
The book that we have sent him yesterday will be read by him.
spmock024.explanation:
The subject of the Active voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. The object of the Active voice is changed into subject of the Passive voice. The usage of a 'to be' form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

Preposition "by" is used before the object made in passive voice.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Perfect tense. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Perfect tense.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will have sent that mail. (Active voice)

That mail will have been sent by him. (Passive voice)

The format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

Note: Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

spmock024.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

options: Mary tell me that she has wanted to make a complaint about me.

Mary told me that she wanted to be made a complaint about me.
spmock024.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject +V1st + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The pronouns 'I' and 'you' are changed into 'she' and 'me' respectively.

· The verb 'want' (present simple) is changed into 'wanted' (past simple).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Mary told me that she wanted to make a complaint about me.

Hence, the answer is option c).

spmock024.explanation:

One way of identifying the time clause is that the Time clause always begins with the following: When, whenever, while, as, since, after, before, until, as soon as

For example:

Ayush said to me, "When I saw him, he was working." (Direct Speech)

Ayush told me that when he saw him, he was working. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he' and the possessive determiner 'my' is changed into 'his'.

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): Rajeev said that he met his old friend from high school when he tried to catch a bus.

spmock025.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The company introduced two comprehensive policies this year after extensive consultation with department heads and employee representatives: one on leave
management, which aims to simplify the process of availing leaves, and the other on performance appraisal, which focuses on evaluating employees fairly
and systematically; the later, which was drafted after careful analysis of previous appraisal challenges, aims to reward deserving employees more effectively
spmock025.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) – Replace “later” with “latter”.

Rule / Concept: Later vs. Latter

Later → Refers to time (afterward, afterwards).

Latter → Refers to the second of two things mentioned.

Trap: In SSC CGL long sentences, candidates often use “later” when referring to the second item instead of “latter”.

Application to the Given Question - Here, “the later” is incorrectly used. It refers to the second policy, performance appraisal, so the correct word is “the latter”.

More Examples for Clarity -

I bought two books: one on history and the other on economics; the latter is more interesting.

The team analyzed two strategies: one for marketing and the other for operations; the latter proved more effective.

Two candidates were shortlisted: Ankit and Ravi; the latter will be interviewed first.

Incorrect Usage -

I met two candidates; the later will be interviewed first.

The company introduced two policies; the later focuses on appraisal.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Check if the word refers to time (later) or the second of two things (latter).

SSC CGL traps often appear in long sentences with semicolons or multiple clauses.

spmock026.explanation:
In a passive voice sentence, the subject in the given active voice sentence becomes the object in the passive voice sentence and the object in an active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.

The tense remains the same in both the active and passive voice sentences and in the passive voice sentence the doer of the action is denoted with the help of the preposition 'by'.

The format of a passive voice sentence is: Subject + Verb + by + Object.

In the active voice, the tense is Past continuous which remains the same in the passive voice too.

In options (b) and (d), the tense of the passive voice sentences is 'Present continuous' and 'Present Perfect tense', respectively, so they are negated. In option (c), the verb 'was' in the second sentence is incorrect as the verb corresponds to a singular noun, but 'some' is a plural pronoun. So, option (c) is also negated.

Option (a) 'Oranges were being sold by a woman. Some of them were being bought by us from the woman' is the correct form of the passive voice sentence, which follows the required grammatical norms of a passive voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

My father told me that honesty is the best policy.
My father has told me that honesty is the best policy.
spmock026.explanation:
The correct answer is Option D: My father has told me that honesty is the best policy.

Key Points

  • Reporting Verb in Present Perfect: The reporting verb "has said to" is in the Present Perfect tense.

    • Rule: If the reporting verb is in the Present (e.g., says), Present Perfect (e.g., has said), or Future (e.g., will say), the tense of the verb in the reported speech does not change.

  • Reporting Verb Change: Just like "said to" changes to "told," the phrase "has said to" changes to "has told" when followed by an object ("me").

  • Universal Truth/Proverb: The statement "Honesty is the best policy" is a universal truth or a proverb.

    • Rule: Even if the reporting verb were in the past tense (e.g., said), the tense of a universal truth or proverb typically remains in the Simple Present.

  • Eliminating Incorrect Options:

    • Option A is incorrect because it changes the tense of the proverb to the past ("was").

    • Option C is incorrect because it changes the reporting verb from Present Perfect ("has told") to Simple Past ("told").

    • Option B is incorrect because "had said to me" should be changed to the more appropriate "had told me" in indirect speech.

spmock026.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: His detailed explanation of the new company policy during the quarterly review
meeting was relatively clear than the one provided by his colleagues, which
helped the team to implement the changes without any confusion.
spmock026.explanation:
The Correct Answer is Option (D) - No Error.

Rule/Concept: Use of Relative and Comparatively -

Words like relative and comparatively already indicate a comparison. Therefore, any adjective following them must be in positive degree. Using a comparative (e.g., clearer, better, higher) after these words is grammatically incorrect.

Application to the Given Question - "His detailed explanation of the new company policy during the quarterly review meeting was relatively clear than the one provided by his colleagues…"

Here, relatively implies the comparison.

Clear is a positive degree adjective, which is correct after relatively.

More Examples for Clarity -

The project is comparatively important for the organization.

His answer was relatively simple for everyone to understand.

This method is comparatively effective in reducing errors.

Incorrect Usage -

The instructions were relatively easier than expected.

The movie was comparatively better than the previous one.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Always use positive degree after relative or comparatively.

Avoid redundancy; comparative degree after these words is trapped in SSC CGL exams.

In long sentences, check the adjective immediately following relative/comparatively.

Our jewels will be asked to be submitted by all of us.
spmock027.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb 'were' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Once upon a time, in a grand estate perched on a hill, there lived an arrogant woman named Victoria. Victoria had recently married a wealthy widower, becoming the stepmother to his young son, Thomas. Her arrival brought an air of entitlement and superiority that cast a shadow over their once happy home. Victoria saw Thomas as an obstacle to her new life of luxury. She resented his presence, considering him an inconvenience that stood in the way of her ambitions. Thomas, despite his tender age, possessed a resilient spirit. He yearned for his father's love and acceptance, but Victoria's coldness only incited his determination to rise above her contemptuous behaviour. He sought solace in his own imagination, finding refuge in books and daydreams that transported him far away from the reality of their toxic household.

Victoria's arrogance began to crumble as she witnessed the positive impact Thomas had on others. She saw his unwavering kindness and the light he brought into their home. Slowly, her heart softened, and she realized the error of her ways. Regret filled her as she reflected on the years of mistreatment and the missed opportunities to build a genuine bond with Thomas. In a moment of vulnerability, Victoria approached Thomas, seeking forgiveness for her past actions. With tears in her eyes, she expressed her remorse and acknowledged the hurt she had caused. Thomas, in a display of grace beyond his years, embraced her with forgiveness, understanding that everyone deserves a chance to change.

From that day forward, Victoria and Thomas worked to rebuild their relationship. Their story became a testament to the transformative power of humility and forgiveness. Victoria learned that true strength lies not in arrogance, but in the ability to acknowledge one's mistakes and grow from them. And Thomas, through his resilience and capacity for forgiveness, showed that love can prevail, even in the face of adversity. In the end, their journey together taught them both valuable lessons about the importance of compassion, empathy, and the capacity for change.

spmock027.explanation:
Expository Passage: This passage provides information or explains a concept or idea. It presents facts, evidence, or arguments in a logical and organized manner to educate or inform the reader.

Persuasive Passage: This passage aims to convince or persuade the reader to adopt a particular viewpoint or take a specific action. It often utilizes rhetorical devices, emotional appeals, and logical reasoning to make a persuasive argument.

Narrative Passage: This passage tells a story or recounts a sequence of events. It typically includes characters, and a plot, and may have a specific narrative structure, such as an introduction, rising action, climax, and resolution.

Reflective Passage: This passage involves introspection or personal reflection on experiences, thoughts, or emotions. It delves into the writer's inner thoughts and feelings, often offering insights or lessons learned.

They cohabit twice in a year and give birth twice in a year. Prior to independence, this antelope was extensively hunted which affected their population so much that this species has reached the stage of extinction in many parts of the country. Poachers kill them mainly for material gain. Its skin has an enormous value in the market. In order to protect this species, the IUCN has declared this species nearly threatened. The author told his assistant that the research summary is completed.
The author told his assistant that the research summary will be completed.
spmock028.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

The Present tense verb 'is' becomes the past tense verb 'was' and 'said to' becomes 'told'.

Accordingly, the correct form of Indirect speech for the sentence is given in option (b), "The author told his assistant that the research summary was completed".

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

spmock028.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: Provided that the weather will remain
clear tomorrow morning, the hikers will
attempt to reach the summit of the peak.
spmock028.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “will remain” with “remains”.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Conditional Clause Restriction

In a First Conditional sentence (which talks about real or possible future events), the sentence is divided into two parts:

  1. The Condition (The "If/Provided that" part): Must be in Simple Present Tense (V1/V{s/es}).

  2. The Result (The "Will" part): Must be in Simple Future Tense (will + V1).

Even though the "weather remaining clear" is something that will happen in the future, the conjunction "Provided that" (which works just like "If") locks the verb into the Present Tense.

💢 Application to the Question

"Provided that the weather will remain clear tomorrow... the hikers will attempt..."

  • The Error: Using "will" twice. You cannot have "will" in the conditional clause and the main clause simultaneously.

  • The Logic: The condition "weather remains clear" is treated as a present requirement for the future action "will attempt" to happen.

  • The Subject: Since "the weather" is an uncountable/singular noun, we use the singular verb form "remains."

Corrected Sentence

Provided that the weather remains clear tomorrow morning, the hikers will attempt to reach the summit of the peak.

🧠 Exam Tip: The "Future Conjunction" List

Whenever you see these words, scan the verb immediately following them. If it has a "will" or "shall," it's almost certainly an error:

  • If / Provided that / Supposing

  • When / As soon as / Before / After

  • Until / Unless / In case

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

spmock030.word:
Mental health has increasingly entered public discourse, yet its inclusion often remains superficial rather than transformative. Awareness campaigns proliferate, terminology becomes more familiar, and institutions adopt symbolic gestures of concern. However, beneath this apparent progress lies a persistent reluctance to confront the structural and cultural conditions that generate psychological distress. Mental health is frequently treated as an individual malfunction, detached from social environments that normalize chronic stress, insecurity, and emotional suppression. This individualized framing carries subtle consequences. When distress is reduced to personal resilience or chemical imbalance, responsibility quietly shifts away from workplaces, educational systems, and economic arrangements that perpetuate exhaustion and precarity. Coping mechanisms are emphasized over prevention, and adaptation is rewarded more than dissent. In such a framework, the mentally healthy individual is not one who is free from distress, but one who can continue functioning despite it. Institutional responses often mirror this logic. Support systems exist, but access is conditional, fragmented, and reactive. Interventions are triggered once productivity declines or visible crisis emerges, rather than when early signs of strain appear. Moreover, the language of wellness is frequently co-opted to enhance performance rather than well-being, blurring the line between care and control. As a result, mental health initiatives risk becoming tools for sustaining existing norms rather than questioning them. The deeper challenge, therefore, lies in redefining mental health beyond the absence of disorder. It demands recognition of emotional suffering as a rational response to irrational conditions. Without this shift, societies may continue to expand mental health services while simultaneously reproducing the very pressures that make such services indispensable.

Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the passage?
options: When Awareness Fails to Address the Roots of Mental Distress
The Rise of Mental Health Campaigns in Modern Society
Psychological Disorders and Individual Responsibility
Institutional Approaches to Emotional Well-Being
spmock030.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - When Awareness Fails to Address the Roots of Mental Distress.

Explanation:

spmock031.word:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in superlative degree of comparison.

options: He is faster than any runner.

spmock031.explanation:
The adjective is 'fast' and it is in the positive degree, which means it does not show any comparison. To change a sentence from the positive degree to the superlative degree, we need to add -est to the adjective and use the definite article 'the' before it. The superlative degree shows that something or someone has the highest degree of quality among all the others in a group.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Option (b) is in comparative degree.

Option (c) is incorrect as 'faster' is in the comparative degree while the positive degree is used with 'as...as'.

Note:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we remove the inverted commas and add the conjunction "If" or "Whether" in the Indirect Speech and the verb/s "Is/are/am/was/were" before the subject, in Direct Speech.

For example:

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Perfect tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Present Perfect tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Asked if - Asked

spmock031.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Chris said to Mary, "Get the dog in the flat before I throw it through this window."
options: Chris ordered Mary to get the dog in the flat before he threw it through that window.
Chris ordered Mary to get the dog in the flat before I threw that through this window.
Chris requested Mary to get the dog in the flat before him threw it through that window.
Chris ordered Mary to get the dog in the flat before him to throw it through that window.
spmock031.explanation:
Imperative Sentences are used to demonstrate Request, Order, Command, etc.

Imperative Sentences begin with Principal verbs like Go, Make, etc.

As per the meaning of "Said", "Say", etc. the verbs changes forms like "begged/beg" etc.

'To' is used before the Principal Verbs in the Indirect Speech.

For example:

John said to his assistant, "Bring a glass of water." (Direct Speech)

John ordered his assistant to bring him a glass of water. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'ordered'.

· The verb 'get' is changed into the infinitive 'to get'.

· The verb 'throw' (simple present) is changed into 'threw' (simple past).

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

· 'This window' is changed into 'that window'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Chris ordered Mary to get the dog in the flat before he threw it through that window.

Hence, the answer is option a).

Note:

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

📌 Rule / Concept: Inverted Subject-Verb Agreement (There) -

In most English sentences, the subject comes first. However, in sentences beginning with "There," the subject is postponed (it comes after the verb). The verb must still agree with that real subject.

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the word "There" is just a filler. To find the real subject, look after the verb: "several unanswered questions." Since "questions" is a plural countable noun, the verb must also be plural. In the present tense, plural verbs do not take an "s." Therefore, "remains" (singular) must be changed to "remain" (plural).

📌 Rule / Concept: Transitive Stative Verbs – Passive Formation
Even stative verbs like contain, hold, possess can form passive voice if they take a direct object. The standard passive structure in the simple present tense is: Object + is/am/are + V³. However, the preposition used in passive must be idiomatically correct. In the case of “contain,” the natural passive expression uses “contained in” rather than “contained by.”

📌 Application to the Given Question

This corporate locker contains the original title deeds of the property. Here, “contains” is a transitive verb with “the original title deeds of the property” as its object. Since the object exists, passive conversion is possible. The correct passive form is: “The original title deeds of the property are contained in this corporate locker.” Option (A) is grammatically awkward because “contained by” is not idiomatic in this context. Option (C) unnecessarily changes the tense to present perfect. Option (D) is incorrect because transitive stative verbs can form passive constructions.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Stative verbs can form passive if they take a direct object. Maintain the original tense during conversion. Use natural prepositions in passive constructions. Avoid tense shifts unless required.

spmock032.word:
When Arvind accepted the managerial position at a declining textile firm, he was aware that the challenge extended far beyond falling profits. The company’s real ailment lay buried in its culture—an unspoken resistance to accountability that had slowly normalized mediocrity. Employees met deadlines just well enough to avoid reprimand, innovation was quietly discouraged under the guise of “practicality,” and senior leadership equated stability with stagnation. Arvind initially chose restraint over disruption, believing that trust must precede transformation. However, this cautious approach was soon misinterpreted as indecision, reinforcing the very complacency he intended to dismantle.

As months passed, subtle patterns emerged. Suggestions were applauded in meetings but ignored in execution, data was selectively presented to justify inaction, and failures were attributed to external forces rather than internal inefficiencies. Arvind realized that the organization did not lack talent; it lacked the discomfort necessary for growth. When he finally introduced performance-linked evaluations and transparent reporting mechanisms, resistance intensified. Critics accused him of eroding harmony and imposing corporate rigidity on a “family-like” workplace. Yet beneath these objections lay a deeper fear—the loss of anonymity in collective failure. The turning point came not through dramatic reform but through consistency. Arvind refused to reverse decisions despite mounting pressure, yet he also resisted authoritarian impulses. Over time, clarity replaced confusion. While some employees exited, others adapted, discovering that accountability, though unsettling, offered professional dignity. The firm did not transform overnight, nor did it achieve spectacular success. But it shed its illusion of comfort, replacing it with a fragile yet honest culture—one where progress was measured not by immediate results, but by the willingness to confront inconvenient truths.

What was the primary reason behind resistance to performance-linked evaluations?
options: Concern that such systems would damage workplace relationships
Fear of external scrutiny and loss of competitive secrecy
Anxiety over exposure of individual accountability
Discomfort with standardized corporate practices
spmock032.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - Anxiety over exposure of individual accountability.

Explanation:
The passage reveals that objections masked a deeper fear—the loss of anonymity in collective failure. Performance evaluations threatened to assign responsibility clearly, which unsettled those accustomed to shared blame.

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG:
A reflects the surface argument but not the underlying motive.
B is incorrect as external scrutiny is never mentioned.
D is partially relevant but too general; the resistance stemmed from accountability, not corporate structure alone.

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Participle (V{ing}) vs. Past Participle (V3)

Participles act as adjectives to describe a noun. Choosing between the -ing and the -ed/V3 form depends on whether the noun is the doer (Active) or the receiver (Passive) of the action.

  • Present Participle (V{ing}): Used when the noun performs the action.

    • Example: A crying baby (The baby is doing the crying).

  • Past Participle (V3): Used when the noun receives the action or is in a particular state because of the action.

    • Example: A broken vase (The vase received the action of breaking).

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...only vaccinating employees are allowed to enter..."

In this sentence, the word "employees" is the noun being described.

  • If we say "vaccinating employees," it means the employees are currently giving vaccines to other people (like doctors or nurses).

  • If we say "vaccinated employees," it means the employees have received the vaccine themselves.

Since the safety regulation is about who is protected against the virus to enter a building, we need the passive form. The employees received the vaccine; therefore, they are vaccinated.

Corrected Sentence

As per the newly updated safety regulations introduced by the government, only vaccinated employees are allowed to enter the corporate building.

Note:

In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

Key Points

  • Indirect Speech: The reporting verb "said to" changes to "told" because it is followed by an object ("the team").

  • Key Conversions:

    • "If you win the match" becomes "If they won that match": The conditional clause in Simple Present ("win") is changed to Simple Past ("won") to match the indirect speech timeline.

    • "this" becomes "that": The demonstrative "this" changes to "that" in indirect speech.

    • "I will give" becomes "he would give": The first-person pronoun "I" changes to "he" (referring to the coach), and the future "will" changes to its past form "would".

  • Pronoun Change: The second-person pronoun "you" refers to the "team" (plural), so it changes to "they" (subject) and "them" (object) in Indirect Speech.

  • Structural Integrity: Option C is the only one that correctly applies the backshift to both the conditional "if" clause and the main clause while maintaining correct pronoun agreement.

In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

options: She said that while she was cooking the dinner, her brother was watching the match.

She said that while she cooked the dinner, her brother watched the match.
spmock034.explanation:
The correct answer is Option A: She said that while she was cooking the dinner, her brother was watching the match.

Key Points

  • Identification of Simultaneous Action: The word "while" indicates that both actions were occurring at the same moment.

  • The "No-Shift" Exception: Even though the reporting verb ("said") is in the past, we do not shift the Past Continuous to Past Perfect Continuous when two such actions are parallel.

  • Tense Maintenance:

    • "was cooking" remains "was cooking".

    • "was watching" remains "was watching".

  • Eliminating Incorrect Options:

    • Option B is a trap because it applies the standard backshift rule (Past Continuous ->Past Perfect Continuous), which shouldn't happen here.

    • Option C is inconsistent, changing only one half of the sentence.

    • Option D changes the tense to Simple Past, which loses the "continuous" meaning of the original sentence.

Option b): Incorrect because "and to his delight, the food was exceptional" precedes "he decided to try a new restaurant yesterday," which disrupts the sequence of events.

spmock035.word: Describe how you will say to your colleague You are wanted by the manager in active voice.
spmock035.explanation:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the verb 'are' and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Indefinite tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

For example:

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

She likes you. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

spmock035.word: Select the option with the correct use of the past perfect tense.
options: I was living in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
I lived in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
I had living in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
I had lived in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
spmock035.explanation:
The past perfect tense is used to talk about an action that happened before another action in the past. In this sentence, the action "had lived in the city" occurred before the action "moved to the countryside".

Option (a)- This uses the past continuous tense, which is incorrect in this context.

Option (b)- This uses the simple past tense, which is incorrect in this context.

Option (c) - This uses the past perfect tense in partially correct form, as the verb "live" should be in the past participle form "lived" instead of the -ing form "living", and the form should be "had lived" instead of "had living".

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object) should be converted into Present Conditional (Subject + would/should + V1 +object).

For example:

He said that he would be in Kolkata on Friday. (Indirect Speech)
