spmock091.word:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

This is one of the best suggestions / that has ever been made / in this committee's history.
options: This is one of the best suggestions
spmock091.explanation:
The error is in the part "that has ever been made".

In sentences containing the structure "one of the + [plural noun] + that/who/which", the verb after the relative pronoun (that, who, which) agrees with the antecedent of the pronoun. Here, the relative pronoun "that" refers to "suggestions," which is a plural noun. Therefore, the verb should also be plural. The singular verb "has" should be replaced with the plural verb "have".

Correct Sentence: This is one of the best suggestions that have ever been made in this committee's history.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

· Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

spmock091.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: Hardly he attended the weekly strategy briefings
during his tenure as the project manager, which eventually
led to several critical lapses in the final execution of the plan.
No Error
spmock091.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “he attended” with “did he attend”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with Adverb of Frequency (Hardly)

When a sentence begins with a negative adverb of frequency like Hardly, Scarcely, or Barely, the sentence must follow the rule of Partial Inversion. Even if the sentence is a simple statement about a habit or a past action (and not part of the "Hardly... when" conjunction pair), the auxiliary verb must come before the subject.

If the sentence is in the Simple Past tense (like "attended"), we must use the auxiliary verb "did" and change the main verb to its base form.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Hardly he attended the weekly strategy briefings...

In this sentence, the word "Hardly" is used at the beginning for emphasis. The verb "attended" is in the Simple Past. To satisfy the rule of inversion, we must introduce the auxiliary verb "did" before the subject "he" and change "attended" to its base form "attend".

Corrected Sentence

Hardly did he attend the weekly strategy briefings during his tenure as the project manager, which eventually led to several critical lapses in the final execution of the plan.

spmock091.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

Sometimes the fog is so ______ that these lights cannot be ______, but most lighthouses _______ great fog bells or fog horns; some of the latter are made to sound by steam and can be ________ for a long distance.
spmock091.explanation:
The sentence talks about how lighthouses work.

In blank 1, all the adjectives are qualifying the noun 'fog' so all can fit here.

In blank 2, 'lights cannot be heard' is an illogical statement, thus, option (d) is eliminated.

In blank 3, 'lighthouses' is a plural noun so the use of the singular verb 'has' is incorrect, a plural verb will be used here, thus option (c) is eliminated.

In blank 4, 'Modal + be' is always followed by a participle form of verb so the use of the base verb 'gather' is incorrect.

'Dense, seen, have, heard' is the right set of words for the blanks.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

NOTE-

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

1. Carry out (पूरा करना / कार्यान्वित करना)

Example 1: It was a difficult speech, but he carried it off with great confidence. (यह एक कठिन भाषण था, लेकिन उसने इसे आत्मविश्वास के साथ सफलतापूर्वक पूरा किया।)

spmock091.word: Nobody in the department was willing to accept responsibility for the lapse, ______?
options: were they
was he
did they
wasn’t he
spmock091.explanation:
👉 The correct answer is - “were they”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Indefinite Pronoun + Auxiliary Repetition Rule

Words like nobody, no one, none make a sentence negative in meaning. When the statement is negative → the tag must be positive.

Also, when the main clause already contains an auxiliary verb (is/was/were/has/have etc.), we must repeat the same auxiliary in the tag.

For indefinite pronouns referring to persons, the tag pronoun is they.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Nobody in the department was willing to accept responsibility for the lapse

  • “Nobody” → negative meaning

  • So, the tag must be positive

  • The auxiliary used in the main clause is was

  • Since the pronoun in the tag is they, the auxiliary changes to were

Therefore: were they?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ - Nobody was present at the venue, were they?

Example 2 ✅ - No one was prepared for the inspection, were they?

Example 3 ✅ - None of the employees was informed earlier, were they?

🧠 Things to Remember

If auxiliary is already present → repeat it in the tag.

  • Nobody / No one → use “they” in tag.

  • Negative meaning → positive tag.

  • Avoid unnecessary do-support.

spmock091.word:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The collection of sculptures is displayed on the museum, showcasing rare and historical pieces from different eras and cultures.
options: The collection of sculptures is displayed
spmock091.explanation:
The error lies in the preposition "on" in the phrase "on the museum." The preposition "on" typically indicates placement on top of a surface, such as "on the table" or "on the wall." In this case, sculptures are not physically placed on the museum building. Instead, they are displayed within the museum's interior space.

Use "in" to indicate that the collection is inside the museum, where the sculptures are being exhibited. This is the most appropriate option since sculptures are displayed within the space of the museum.

"At" can also be used when you want to refer to a specific location, like a building or venue, without focusing on whether it's inside or outside. Example: "The collection of sculptures is displayed at the museum."

So, the correct sentence is: The collection of sculptures is displayed in/at the museum, showcasing rare and historical pieces from different eras and cultures.

spmock092.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The archaeological survey team discovered
a most remarkable series of inscriptions
buried deep within the cavern’s walls.
No Error
spmock092.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (D)

👉 No replacement required.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Use of "A Most"

the superlative word "most" is usually preceded by the definite article the when it is used to compare three or more things (e.g., "the most beautiful city in the world"). However, "most" can also be used as an adverb meaning "very" or "exceedingly." When "most" is used in this sense to provide emphasis rather than to make a direct comparison, it is preceded by the indefinite article a. [ In short; A MOST = VERY ]

💢 Application to the Given Question

(a most remarkable series of inscriptions)

In this sentence, the speaker is not comparing these inscriptions to all other inscriptions in the world to find a "winner." Instead, they are simply stating that the inscriptions were very remarkable. Therefore, "a most" is grammatically correct and appropriate for the context.



Corrected Sentence

The archaeological survey team discovered a most remarkable series of inscriptions buried deep within the cavern’s walls.

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 This is a most interesting story you have shared with us. (Meaning: a very interesting story) ✅

Example 2 Mr. Khanna is a most diligent employee. (Meaning: a very diligent employee) ✅

❌ Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1 He is the most kind man I met yesterday. (Unless comparing him to all men ever met, use "a most" for "a very"). ❌

Wrong example 2 It was a most tallest building in the city. ("Most" cannot be used with an "-est" adjective; this is a double superlative error). ❌

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • Comparison vs. Description: If the sentence ends with a comparison group (e.g., "in the class," "of the two," "in the world"), use The Most. If it is just a descriptive statement of quality, A Most is often the intended "trappy" correct answer.

  • The "Very" Test: If you can replace "most" with "very" and the sentence makes perfect sense without needing a comparison, "A Most" is correct.

spmock092.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

"was getting" changes to "is getting".

"Divide" means to separate into parts or groups. While dividing is related to separation, it does not fit well with the context of microorganisms surviving and functioning in an oxygen-free environment. The focus here is on survival and activity, not separation.

"Recede" means to move back or withdraw. It is not related to the behaviour of microorganisms in the context of producing biogas. "Recede" does not fit the context of survival and activity in an oxygen-free environment.

"Convince" means to persuade someone to do something or believe something. It is unrelated to the context of microorganisms or their behaviour in an oxygen-free environment.

In Active voice (look at the options), it should be an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

Do
Does

spmock093.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The hen had lain several eggs
in the corner of the barn before
the farmer arrived this morning.
No Error
spmock093.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (A).

Replace “lain” with “laid”.

📌 Rule/Concept: Transitive vs. Intransitive Verbs (Lie vs. Lay) -

The confusion arises because the past tense of "Lie" is "Lay." However, they are two distinct verbs:

Lie (Intransitive): To recline or be in a flat position. It does not take an object.

Forms: Lie (V1), Lay (V2), Lain (V3), Lying (V-ing).

Lay (Transitive): To put or place something down. It must have an object.

Forms: Lay (V1), Laid (V2), Laid (V3), Laying (V-ing).

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, "several eggs" is the direct object receiving the action of being placed or produced. Therefore, we must use the transitive verb Lay. Since the sentence uses the past perfect tense ("had" + V3), we need the V3 form of "Lay," which is Laid. "Lain" is the V3 of the intransitive verb "Lie" (to recline), which is incorrect here.

More Examples for Clarity -

1- He laid his coat on the bed. (Object: coat)

2- I have lain on this sofa for three hours. (No object; reclining)

3- Please lay the book on the shelf. (Object: book).

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Object Check: If there is a noun/pronoun after the verb (eggs, stress, foundation, book), use Lay/Laid/Laid.

The V3 Trap: Remember that Lain is for resting/reclining, and Laid is for putting/placing.

Action Type: "Lay" requires an actor putting something somewhere. "Lie" describes the state of the subject itself.

spmock093.word:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.

The plumber/ fixed the leak (A)/ after the water (B)/ had flood (C)/ the basement. / No error (D).
spmock093.explanation:
The erroneous part in the sentence is (C). The error in segment (C) relates to the verb tense agreement. The sentence describes two past actions: the flooding of the basement and the plumber fixing the leak. The sequence of events indicates that the flooding occurred before the plumber fixed the leak. To express this sequence of events properly, the past perfect tense is used to indicate an action that occurred before another past action. In this case, "had flooded" (past participle form (V3)) should be used instead of "had flood" (flood is the base form of the verb) to convey that the flooding happened prior to the plumber fixing the leak. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: "The plumber fixed the leak after the water had flooded the basement."

spmock093.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: After the severe hailstorm damaged the
warehouse roof, the manager got the entire
structure repair by a team of specialized contractors.
spmock093.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “repair” with “repaired”.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Causative Passive

Sub + get/have + object + past participle + by + real doer

When we use verbs like Have or Get to show that someone else performed a task for us, the grammar depends entirely on what follows the verb. If a thing/object (the receiver) comes first, we must use the Past Participle (V3).

The Logic:

  • Active: The manager got the contractors (People) to repair the roof.

  • Passive: The manager got the roof (Object) repaired.

In the passive version, we don't care who did it as much as what was done to the object.

💢 Application to the Given Question

The sentence is designed to overwhelm you with descriptive clauses ("After the severe hailstorm," "team of specialized contractors"), but the core error is found in the causative link:

"...got the entire structure (Object) repair (Incorrect Verb Form)..."

  1. The Causative Verb: "Got"

  2. The Object: "The entire structure" (The warehouse roof/building).

  3. The Action: "Repair."

Since the "structure" cannot repair itself, the relationship is passive. the verb "repair" must be changed to its third form, "repaired."

Corrected sentence

After the severe hailstorm damaged the warehouse roof, the manager got the entire structure repaired by a team of specialized contractors.

More Examples for Clarity

  • Example 1: I had my hair cut yesterday. (Not cutted or to cut).

  • Example 2: She got her laptop fixed at the service center. (Not fix).

  • Example 3: You should have your eyes tested regularly. (Not test).

I would have delegated a little more

than the project manager did

No error
spmock094.explanation:
Option A — replace “were” with “had been”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Third Conditional (Unreal Past Condition)

This sentence refers to:

  • a completed project in the past
  • a hypothetical situation contrary to fact

The correct conditional structure for unreal past situations is:

If + had been / had + V³ → would have + V³

💢 Application to the Given Question

“the last project”

  • Clearly refers to a finished past event
  • Hence, the condition must be located in the past unreal

“would have delegated”

  • Correct third-conditional result form
  • Already fixed in the past hypothetical frame

Therefore:

  • if I had been in charge ✅
  • if I were in charge ❌ (this form is for unreal present, not unreal past)

Since the result clause is already correct, the only error lies in Part A.

spmock094.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

A woman was selling oranges. We were buying some of them from the woman.
options: Oranges were being sold by a woman. Some of them were being bought by us from the woman.
Oranges are being sold by the woman. Some of them are being bought by us from the woman.
Oranges were being sold by a woman. Some of them was bought by us from the woman.
Oranges have been sold by a woman. Some of them have been bought by us from the woman.
spmock094.explanation:
In a passive voice sentence, the subject in the given active voice sentence becomes the object in the passive voice sentence and the object in an active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.

The tense remains the same in both the active and passive voice sentences and in the passive voice sentence the doer of the action is denoted with the help of the preposition 'by'.

The format of a passive voice sentence is: Subject + Verb + by + Object.

In the active voice, the tense is Past continuous which remains the same in the passive voice too.

In options (b) and (d), the tense of the passive voice sentences is 'Present continuous' and 'Present Perfect tense', respectively, so they are negated. In option (c), the verb 'was' in the second sentence is incorrect as the verb corresponds to a singular noun, but 'some' is a plural pronoun. So, option (c) is also negated.

Option (a) 'Oranges were being sold by a woman. Some of them were being bought by us from the woman' is the correct form of the passive voice sentence, which follows the required grammatical norms of a passive voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

Words like including, excluding, besides, between, but (when it means 'except'), like, and unlike often function as prepositions. In English grammar, any pronoun that follows a preposition must be in the Objective Case.

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the word "including" acts as a preposition. Therefore, the pronouns following it must be in the objective case. While "she" is the subjective form "her" is the objective form.

spmock094.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: Despite the widespread implementation of several modern farming techniques and
subsidies, the peasantry of this drought-stricken region is still struggling
to repay the high-interest loans taken from local moneylenders.
No Error
spmock094.explanation:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B).

Replace “is” with “are”.

Rule/Concept: Nouns Singular in Form but Plural in Meaning -

Certain collective nouns such as Peasantry, Gentry, Clergy, Poultry, Cattle, and Police - do not end in ‘s’, yet they represent a group or class of individuals. These nouns are always considered plural and must be followed by a plural verb. In this context, "Peasantry" refers to the class of small farmers or agricultural laborers as a whole. Although it appears singular in form (lacking an 's'), it refers to a collective group of people. Therefore, the singular auxiliary verb "is" is grammatically incorrect. It must be replaced with the plural verb "are" to achieve proper subject-verb agreement

Corrected Sentence - Despite the widespread implementation of several modern farming techniques and subsidies, the peasantry of this drought-stricken region are still struggling to repay the high-interest loans taken from local moneylenders.

Only highly trained officials were allowed to access the confidential records stored in the digital archive.

What kind of officials? → highly trained officials

spmock094.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: With a view to enhance the aesthetic
appeal of the heritage site, the government
sanctioned a massive renovation budget.
spmock094.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “enhance” with “enhancing”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Gerunds after "With a view to"

In English grammar, the phrase "With a view to" is a compound preposition used to express a purpose or intention. Unlike the standard infinitive marker "to" (which is followed by V1), the "to" in this specific phrase is a preposition. A preposition must be followed by a Noun or a Gerund (V{ing} used as a noun).

REMEMBER THE LIST

Use gerund or nouns after these phrases or adjectives: Look forward to, With a view to, In addition to, Pay attention to, Conducive to, Accustomed to, Prone to, Vulnerable to, Addicted to, Devoted to, Indifferent to, Object to, Averse to, Opposed to, (Prefer to) etc

💢 Application to the Given Question

"With a view to enhance the aesthetic appeal..."

In this sentence, "With a view to" functions as a fixed prepositional phrase. Following the grammatical requirement of this phrase, the verb "enhance" must be converted into its gerund form, "enhancing," to serve as the object of the preposition.

Corrected Sentence

With a view to enhancing the aesthetic appeal of the heritage site, the government sanctioned a massive renovation budget.

spmock094.word: Describe how you will say The large pill might be swallowed by him in active voice.
options: He might have swallowed the large pill.
He might be swallowing the large pill.
He might swallow the large pill.
He might swallowed the large pill.
spmock094.explanation:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb 'be' and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs and they should be used correctly as stated below.

Some of the modal verbs are: Can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of such a sentence in Active voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

For example:

This can be done by you. (Passive Voice)

You can do this. (Active Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

spmock094.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The legendary artist painted
in his private studio passionately
every morning before the sunrise.
No Error
spmock094.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “in his private studio passionately” with “passionately in his private studio”.

Rule / Concept: The M-P-T Rule (Sequence of Adverbs)

When a sentence contains multiple adverbs or adverbial phrases—specifically Adverb of Manner (how), Adverb of Place (where), and Adverb of Time (when)—they must follow a specific chronological order: Manner → Place → Time (M-P-T).

Application to the Given Question

"...painted in his private studio passionately every morning..."

In this sentence, we have three distinct adverbial components:

  1. Place: in his private studio

  2. Manner: passionately

  3. Time: every morning

The current structure follows a P-M-T order, which is grammatically incorrect. According to the MPT rule, the adverb of manner ("passionately") must come first, followed by the place ("in his private studio"), and finally the time ("every morning").

Corrected Sentence

The legendary artist painted passionately in his private studio every morning before the sunrise.



More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: She danced gracefully (M) on the stage (P) last night (T). ✅

Example 2: He spoke earnestly (M) at the meeting (P) this morning (T). ✅

Example 3: The children played happily (M) in the garden (P) all afternoon (T). ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1: She danced last night gracefully on the stage. (T-M-P) ❌

Wrong example 2: He spoke at the meeting earnestly this morning. (P-M-T) ❌

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • The MPT Formula: Memorize the acronym MPT as if it were a mathematical formula for sentence construction.

  • Verb of Movement Exception: If the verb indicates movement (e.g., go, come, arrive, reach), the order often shifts to P-M-T (e.g., "He went to Delhi [P] by train [M] yesterday [T]"). However, for standard action verbs, stick strictly to M-P-T.



Some verbs don’t follow MPT rule.

(go, come, arrive, reach etc.)

spmock094.word:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence:

Through the dense forest, / the hikers / trekked / for hours / before reaching / the mountain peak.
options: The hikers for hours through the dense forest trekked before reaching the mountain peak.
The hikers trekked for hours through the dense forest before reaching the mountain peak.
Through the dense forest for hours trekked the hikers before reaching the mountain peak.

spmock094.explanation:
A meaningful sentence follows the order: subject->verb->duration->place->conclusion. As per the above order, 'the hikers' is the subject, so it comes as the first part, followed by the verb 'trekked'. The sequence of duration, location and conclusion is "for hours" (time duration), "through the dense forest" (place) and "before reaching the mountain top" (conclusion).

The rearranged sentence: The hikers trekked for hours through the dense forest before reaching the mountain peal.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

spmock094.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: The state government has appointed
several runner-ups of the national
sports meet as junior athletic coaches.
No Error
spmock094.explanation:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B).

Replace “runner-ups” with “runners-up”.

Rule/Concept: Pluralization of Compound Nouns -

-A compound noun is a noun made up of two or more words. To make a compound noun plural, we must identify the root word (the principal or main word) and add 's' to it.

-In the word "runner-up," the main noun is "runner," while "up" is a preposition acting as a modifier. Therefore, the plural form is "runners-up ✅," not "runner-ups. ❌"

Corrected Sentence - The state government has appointed several runners-up of the national sports meet as junior athletic coaches.

More Examples for Clarity -

-All my sons-in-law are professionally successful. ✅

-The hangers-on were waiting outside the celebrity's house. ✅

-Many passers-by witnessed the unusual phenomenon. ✅

spmock094.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said, "I have got a new job" (Direct Speech)

He said that he had got a new job (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"I" becomes "He"

"Have buried" becomes "Had buried" (past perfect)

spmock094.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: In light of the recent economic downturn,
the board of directors may likely postpone
the annual general meeting until the next quarter.
spmock094.explanation:
Replace “may likely postpone” with “may postpone” or “is likely to postpone”.

Rule / Concept: Redundancy of Possibility - In English grammar, the modal verbs 'May' and 'Might' are used to express possibility or likelihood. Similarly, words like 'likely', 'possibly', 'probably', 'perhaps', and 'chance' also denote the same sense of uncertainty. Using a modal of possibility along with an adverb/adjective of possibility in the same clause is redundant (superfluous). You must use one or the other, but never both.

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, "may" already indicates that the postponement is a possibility. Adding "likely" creates a "double possibility" error. To correct it, you should either say "may postpone" or "is likely to postpone."

More Examples for Clarity

  1. It may rain tonight. ✔

  2. It may possibly rain today. ❌

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  1. The "May/Likely" Pair: This is a classic "Superfluous Expression" error frequently tested in SSC Mains.

  2. The "Can/Able" Parallel: Just as "Can + Able" is wrong, "May + Likely/Possibly" is wrong.

  3. Active vs. Passive: "Likely" often requires the "to + V1" structure (e.g., is likely to go), whereas "May" is followed directly by the base form of the verb (e.g., may go)

  4. Don't Over-correct: Students often get so used to spotting "Can be able to" errors that they start marking "May be able to" as an error too. Remember: Possibility (May) + Ability (Be able to) = Correct. It is used for future possibility based on present condition.

spmock094.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

multiple accident victims arrived late at night.
spmock094.explanation:

📌 Rule / Concept: Narrative Tense Consistency

When a sentence describes a specific event that occurred in the past, all the main verbs related to that event must remain in the Simple Past Tense .

If a sentence provides a time-marker in the past (such as "when... arrived"), it establishes a "Past Zone."

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...Dr. Mehta take charge... when multiple accident victims arrived..."

There are two related actions in this sentence:

  1. The victims arrived (Simple Past - $V_2$).

  2. Dr. Mehta take charge (Simple Present - $V_1$).

The word "when" creates a direct temporal link between the two actions. Since the arrival of the victims happened in the past, the act of taking charge must also have happened at that same past moment. Therefore, "take" (Present) must be changed to "took" (Past) to match the narrative context.

Corrected Sentence

afternoon that we
stopped playing.

📌 Rule / Concept: Correlative Conjunctions – Such... that vs. So... that

Both structures are used to express cause and effect or to emphasize the degree of a quality. However, their grammatical application differs based on the parts of speech they modify:

Such + (a/an) + Adjective + Noun + that: "Such" is used to modify a noun or a noun phrase. If the noun is countable and singular, the article "a/an" must be included.

So + Adjective/Adverb + that: "So" is used when modifying an adjective or an adverb directly without a following noun.

Things to Remember:

The Noun Test: If there is a noun following the adjective, use "Such." If the noun is absent, use "So."

Article Check: With "Such," don't forget the article for singular countable nouns (such a mistake, not such mistake).

Intensity vs. Result: In SSC/Banking questions, ensure "that" is present to complete the result clause. Occasionally, examiners replace "that" with "as," which is a common trap.

Rule / Concept: The "Too...To" Negative Result

he combination of Too + Adjective + To-Infinitive implies a negative result or an inability to perform an action.

  • Very simply increases the intensity of the adjective (e.g., very hot).

  • Too indicates that the intensity has reached an excessive or undesirable level that prevents the subsequent action from happening.

TOO :- (more than what is required).It is used

to qualify negative adjectives.

➢ VERY:- It can be used to qualify both positive

and negative adjectives

Application to the Given Question

"...the liquid was very hot to drink comfortably without causing a severe burn..."

Because the sentence describes a situation where drinking the soup would cause a "severe burn" (a negative consequence/inability), the adverb "very" is insufficient. We need "too" to link the extreme heat to the inability to drink it safely.

Corrected Sentence Even though the waiter had warned us that the soup had just been removed from the stove, the liquid was too hot to drink comfortably without causing a severe burn to the tongue.

More Examples for Clarity

  • He is too old to run a marathon. (Negative result: He cannot run) ✅

  • The box is very heavy. (It’s heavy, but I might still lift it) ✅

  • The box is too heavy to lift. (Negative result: I cannot lift it) ✅

The Correct Answer is Option B.

Explanation: In the first sentence, the phrase “contrary to the literature” shows that the statement is not a generally accepted fact, but rather a hypothetical or speculative conclusion based on projections or models. Because of this uncertainty, we use “would” instead of “will” to express a less definite, more tentative result.

So, “will cause” → “would cause”

This use of “would” indicates that the result is conditional, theoretical, or dependent on certain assumptions, which is common in academic and scientific writing.

In the second sentence:

…if we do nothing, climate change (of any kind) will have major effects on our daily lives.

This is a first conditional structure, used to describe a real and likely future consequence.

The correct structure is: if + present simple, will + base verb

 

  • if we do nothing → present simple ✔
  • will have major effects → future simple ✔

So, the second sentence is grammatically correct and needs no change.

📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with "So + Adjective/Adverb of manner"

When a sentence begins with "So + Adjective" or "So + Adverb" to provide emphasis to the degree of an action or quality, the main clause must follow the Inversion structure. This means the auxiliary verb (is, are, was, were, do, does, did, has, have) must be placed before the subject. This structure is typically followed by a "that" clause to show the result.

💢 Application to the Given Question

So rapidly the technological landscape is evolving...

In this sentence, the phrase "So rapidly" (So + Adverb) starts the sentence. According to the rules of emphatic inversion, the auxiliary verb "is" must be moved from its position after the subject ("the technological landscape") to a position before it.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 2 ✅: So huge was the explosion that it could be heard from ten miles away.

📌 Rule / Concept: Modal Verb in Passive Voice (Modal + Be + V³)

When an active sentence contains a modal verb (can, could, may, might, must, should, would, etc.), the passive structure follows a fixed pattern: Modal + be + V³

The modal remains unchanged, and “be” is inserted before the past participle. The main verb changes to its past participle form (V³).

Active Structure: Subject + Modal + V¹ + Object

Passive Structure: Object + Modal + be + V³

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

In modal passive constructions, always insert “be” after the modal. Do not change the modal unless required. Maintain the original tense and modality. Modal + be + V³ is a fixed and highly tested structure in SSC and Banking examinations.

spmock096.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: She was not enough confident
to deliver the speech in front
of such a huge audience.
No error

Concept: The Position of "Enough"

  • With Adjectives/Adverbs: "Enough" must always be placed AFTER the adjective or adverb it modifies ($Adjective/Adverb + Enough$).

  • Correct: Brave enough, fast enough, tall enough.

  • Incorrect: Enough brave, enough fast, enough tall.

  • With Nouns: "Enough" must be placed BEFORE the noun it modifies ($Enough + Noun$).

  • Correct: Enough money, enough time, enough people.

Application to the Given Question

In the sentence:

"She was not enough (Adverb) confident (Adjective)..."

The word "confident" is an adjective describing the subject "She." According to the rule, "enough" must follow the adjective it qualifies

Corrected Sentence

She was not confident enough to deliver the speech in front of such a huge audience.

More Examples for Clarity

  • Adjective: He is strong enough to lift that weight. ✅

  • Adverb: She ran quickly enough to catch the bus. ✅

  • Noun: I have enough gas in the car for the trip.✅



Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • The "Adjective After" Trap: Examiners love to place "enough" before words like brave, kind, intelligent, or lucky. Always check if the word is a quality (adjective); if it is, "enough" must go behind it

spmock096.word:
Select the passive form of the following sentence.

"The new insolvency regulations concern all major credit-lending institutions in the country."
options: All major credit-lending institutions in the country are concerned by the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country are concerned with the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country are being concerned by the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country were concerned with the new insolvency regulations.
spmock096.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

📌 Rule / Concept: Transitive Verb “Concern” – Passive Formation
When “concern” is used as a transitive verb meaning “affect” or “relate to,” it can form a passive construction in the simple present tense. The structure becomes: Object + is/am/are + V³ (+ by + Subject). The tense must remain unchanged during conversion. Note that “concerned with” carries a different meaning (“involved with”) and is not the passive of “concern” in this context.

📌 Application to the Given Question

The new insolvency regulations concern all major credit-lending institutions in the country. Here, “concern” is in the simple present tense and takes “all major credit-lending institutions in the country” as its object. In passive voice, this object becomes the subject. Since it is plural, the correct auxiliary is “are.” The correct passive structure is: are + concerned + by. Option (B) changes the meaning to “involved with.” Option (C) incorrectly shifts to present continuous. Option (D) changes the tense to past.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Maintain the original tense during passive conversion. Be careful with verbs like “concern,” where “concerned with” has a different meaning. Ensure correct subject–verb agreement. Do not shift tense unnecessarily.

Certain stative verbs (verbs describing a state rather than an action) do not take the preposition “by.”

The Rule: Verbs like concern, interest, consist, contain, and know take specific prepositions in their standard constructions. Concerned → with (or about); Interested → in; Consist → of; Known → to; Contained → in.

The Trap: Option (A) is the “Formulaic Trap.” A student applying the mechanical “by” rule blindly in passive formation will choose the wrong answer.

spmock096.word: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options: During the high-stakes quarterly review session, the frustrated
manager shouted in the conference room very angrily when the
junior analysts failed to provide substantial answers to his critical questions.

Concept: The M-P-T Rule (Manner-Place-Time)

In English syntax, when a verb is followed by multiple adverbs, they must be arranged in a specific logical order to maintain formal clarity:

  1. Manner (M): How the action was done (very angrily).

  2. Place (P): Where the action occurred (in the conference room).

  3. Time (T): When the action occurred (during the session).

Application to the Question

Even with the added descriptors ("high-stakes," "quarterly review," "junior analysts"), the grammar error remains in the P-M sequence. To correct it, the adverb of Manner must move before the adverbial phrase of Place.

  • Incorrect (P-M): shouted in the conference room (P) very angrily (M).

  • Correct (M-P): shouted very angrily (M) in the conference room (P).

Corrected Sentence During the high-stakes quarterly review session, the frustrated manager shouted very angrily in the conference room when the junior analysts failed to provide substantial answers to his critical questions.

The "Tomorrow" Factor: In English, the present continuous (is/are + verb-ing) is commonly used to talk about scheduled future actions.

Why (D) "was" is incorrect: "Was" is a singular past tense verb. While it matches the singular subject "group," it contradicts the word "tomorrow," which requires a present or future tense.

spmock096.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

Start the match. (Active)

Let the match be started. (Passive)

The Third Conditional is used to express an unreal or hypothetical situation in the past and its probable past result. When the sentence begins with "Had" (inversion), it replaces the "If + had + V3" structure. The mandatory structure for the result clause is: Had + Subject + V3 (Past Participle) + ..., Subject + would/could/might + have + V3.

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the condition is correctly established using "Had the whistle-blower not leaked..." (an unreal past condition). However, the result clause in Part C uses "would remained," which is grammatically incomplete. To show a past hypothetical result, "would" must be followed by "have" and the past participle (V3) "remained."

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: Had I known about the traffic, I would have started earlier.

Example 2 ✅: Had she studied harder, she might have passed the entrance exam.

Example 3 ✅: The company could have avoided bankruptcy had it diversified its portfolio.

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Past vs. Present Perfect with Specific Time Markers -

The Present Perfect Tense (has/have + V3) is used for actions that happened at an unspecific time or have a direct connection to the present. However, as soon as a specific past time marker (like yesterday, in 1947, in the 18th century, ago) is mentioned, the action is "anchored" in the past and disconnected from the present. In such cases, you must use the Simple Past Tense (V2).

💢 Application to the Given Question - The phrase "in the eighteenth century" is a specific, finished period of time. It acts as a "dead" time marker. Because the sentence specifies exactly when this shaping occurred (a time that is now over), the Present Perfect "have shaped" is grammatically incorrect. It must be changed to the Simple Past "shaped" to match the finished time reference.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: I bought this car in 2015. (Specific year = Simple Past) ✅

Example 2: The Egyptian civilization flourished thousands of years ago. ("Ago" = Simple Past) ✅

When "must" denotes morality or universality, there isn't any change in the use of "must".

For example:

The Professor said, "We must love our country."

For example:

Rahul said, "I must go to school at once."

Rahul said that he had to go to school at once.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

· In the given sentence 'must' doesn't denote universality or morality. So, 'must' will change to 'had to'.

· The pronoun 'I' changes to 'he'.

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

📌 Rule: Parallelism after "To" (Infinitives)

When you use the word "to" to join two or more verbs (to express purpose or intent), it creates an infinitive structure. Both verbs must be in the base form (V1).

The structure is: To + [Base Verb 1] + and + [Base Verb 2].

💢 Analysis of the Options

  • Original Sentence (c): "...to improve (V1) and enhance (V1)..."

    • This is perfectly correct. The "to" applies to both "improve" and "enhance." Think of it as: to improve and (to) enhance.

  • a) have promised to improve and enhanced:

    • Incorrect. This violates the rule of parallelism. You cannot have a V1(improve) and a V2/V3 (enhanced) connected by "and" under the same "to."

  • b) has promised to improve and enhance:

    • Incorrect. The subject is "The university authorities" (plural). Therefore, you must use the plural helping verb "have," not the singular "has."

  • d) have promise to improve and enhance:

    • Incorrect. After the helping verb "have," we must use the Past Participle (V3). It should be "have promised," not "have promise."

spmock097.word:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.

Having being in the company(A)/ for over a decade, / Michael was well-versed in(B)/ the intricacies of the industry/ and had developed strong(C)/ relationships with clients. / No error (D).
spmock097.explanation:
"Having" is a gerund or present participle form of the verb "have," which is used to indicate an ongoing action or state. However, in this context, we need the past participle form of the verb.

"Being" is the present participle, which is used in continuous tenses (e.g., "is being," "was being"), and it's inappropriate here because the sentence refers to a past and completed action.

"Having been" is the correct past perfect participle form, used to indicate a completed action in the past that is relevant to the present or another past event. In this sentence, it implies that Michael's long presence in the company led to his expertise and relationships.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence: Having been in the company for over a decade, Michael was well-versed in the intricacies of the industry and had developed strong relationships with clients.

Note: Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The skill has been perfected by my mentor. I have been shaped by my mentor since my adulthood.

spmock099.explanation:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ('been' in this case) and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Perfect tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object.

For example:

A new horse has been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

Arya has bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

spmock099.word: Although the path was steep and dangerous, __________ the trekkers refused to turn back.
spmock099.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option D

👉 The blank should be filled with “yet”.

📌 Rule / Concept: The "Although... yet" Pair

In formal grammar, Although and Though are correlative conjunctions. They introduce a contrast and must be followed by a specific "partner" word or punctuation to complete the sentence structure.

The Rule: Although/Though must be paired with yet or a comma ( , ).

The Error: Using but with Although is a redundancy error because both words perform the same function (showing contrast).

Why "But" is Wrong:

If you use "but," you are effectively saying: "Even though it was dangerous, BUT they went." This is like using two steering wheels for one car; it is redundant and grammatically "crowded."

✅ Correct Sentence: Although the path was steep and dangerous, yet the trekkers refused to turn back.

📌 Rule / Concept: Mixed Conditional — Past Unreal Cause, Present Real Result

This sentence uses a mixed conditional, where:

  • the if-clause refers to an unreal past condition
  • the main clause states a present, factual outcome

Key point (CGL level): The tense of the result clause is governed by time reference, not by the tense used in the if-clause.

💢 Application to the Given Question

“If the policy had addressed regional disparities earlier,”

  • had addressed → past perfect
  • signals an unreal / contrary-to-fact past condition

“the present implementation ______ far less resistance.”

  • present implementation → explicit present reference
  • The sentence describes what is happening now, not what happened in the past or will happen in the future

Therefore:

  • The result clause must be in the present simple

Hence, faces is correct

Using the definite article "the" before "nation" would not accurately convey the intended meaning of the sentence, which is to highlight India as a nation in general. Instead, the indefinite article "a" is more appropriate in this context to indicate that India is being considered as one among many nations. Sentence D is incorrect because of the use of the indefinite article "an" before "united country." The correct form should use "a" instead of "an." "A" is used before words that begin with a consonant sound, while "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. In the given case, the word "united" starts with a consonant sound. Accordingly, article "a" should be used. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

Note:

The compliance documents were submitted before the deadline expires.
spmock100.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

📌 Rule / Concept: Imperative Sentence in Passive Voice

When an imperative sentence (command/request/order) begins with a base verb, its passive form is generally constructed using:

Let + object + be + V³

Structure:
Active: Verb + object
Passive: Let + object + be + V³

If the imperative is negative, the structure becomes:
Let + object + not be + V³

This structure is standard in formal written English and is frequently tested in SSC and Banking exams.

Here, “Submit” is an imperative verb and “the compliance documents” is the object. To convert into passive, the object becomes the focus, and the structure must follow:

Let + object + be + V³

Therefore, the correct passive form is:
Let the compliance documents be submitted before the deadline expires.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Imperatives always convert using “Let + object + be + V³.” Maintain the command tone. Do not convert it into a simple present statement. Negative imperatives require “not” after the object. This structure is a common direct transformation question in SSC and Banking Mains.

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech

NOTE:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

is

were

Would be

📌 Rule / Concept: First Conditional (Real / Possible Future Condition)

The First Conditional is used to talk about real, possible, and achievable situations in the present or future and their likely results.

Standard Structure:

If + Present Simple → will + base verb

Key point:

 

  • The if-clause states a real condition, not a hypothetical or unreal one.
  • Therefore, it must use a present tense, not a past or modal form.

💢 Application to the Given Question

“If the revised protocol _____ approved by the ethics committee, the study will proceed to the data-collection phase.”

Here:

 

  • Approval by the ethics committee is a real and pending possibility.
  • The result (the study will proceed) is a future action dependent on that approval.

Because the condition is real and open, the correct verb in the if-clause is present simple:

  • “is approved” → grammatically and logically correct.

Why the others fail:

  • were → marks an unreal or hypothetical condition (Second Conditional), which is not intended.
  • had been → shifts the sentence to an unreal past (Third Conditional), which contradicts the future result.
  • would be → modals are not used in the if-clause of standard conditionals.

Logic Breakdown:

(A) Two-thirds of the modern laboratory equipments were broken:

Error: The noun following "of" is "equipment," which is uncountable. Uncountable nouns (like water, milk, or equipment) always require a singular verb.

Correction: ...equipment was broken.

Equipment doesn’t take ‘s’.

(B) The variety of rare postage stamps were lost:

Correction: The variety... was lost.

(C) No worker and no senior clerk was present:

(D) Most of the private digital information were leaked:

Error: The noun following "of" is "information," which is uncountable. Just like equipment, it cannot be pluralized and must take a singular verb.

Correction: ...information was leaked.

spmock102.word:
Banks occupy a paradoxical position in modern economies. They are simultaneously engines of growth and custodians of systemic stability. While their primary function is to allocate capital efficiently, their operations are deeply intertwined with public trust, regulatory oversight, and macroeconomic resilience. This dual role becomes particularly visible during periods of financial stress, when decisions taken in the pursuit of profitability can amplify vulnerabilities rather than mitigate them. One persistent banking challenge lies in the tension between credit expansion and risk containment. In growth phases, banks are incentivized to loosen lending standards to capture market share, often relying heavily on optimistic projections and asset valuations. Such practices appear rational in isolation but collectively generate fragility. When economic conditions reverse, non-performing assets rise, capital buffers erode, and balance sheets reveal risks that were previously obscured by growth narratives. Regulatory interventions, though designed to prevent systemic collapse, introduce their own complications. Compliance requirements increase operational costs and can constrain lending, particularly to small and medium enterprises. Moreover, regulation often responds to past crises, leaving banks to navigate new financial instruments and digital risks with frameworks that lag innovation. This regulatory asymmetry fuels debates over whether banks are being overburdened or insufficiently restrained. Compounding these issues is the evolving relationship between banks and technology. Digitalization promises efficiency, financial inclusion, and real-time risk monitoring. Yet it also concentrates operational risks, exposes systems to cyber threats, and alters the traditional bank–customer relationship. As banks increasingly resemble technology-driven service platforms, questions arise about accountability, resilience, and the adequacy of existing safeguards. Ultimately, banking stability depends not merely on stronger regulations or advanced technology, but on institutional judgment. Without disciplined risk culture and transparent governance, banks may continue oscillating between excess and restraint, reinforcing cycles of confidence and crisis rather than breaking them.

In the sentence
“When economic conditions reverse, non-performing assets rise, capital buffers erode, and balance sheets reveal risks that were previously obscured by growth narratives,”
the clause “that were previously obscured by growth narratives” functions as:
options: An adverbial clause of time
A noun clause acting as an object
A relative clause modifying “risks”
A participial clause indicating cause
spmock102.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - A relative clause modifying “risks”.

Explanation:
The clause provides additional information about “risks,” specifying which risks are being referred to. It directly modifies the noun and is therefore a relative clause.

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG:
A is incorrect because the clause does not indicate time.
B misidentifies the grammatical role of the clause.
D is wrong as the structure is not participial.

spmock102.word:
Banks occupy a paradoxical position in modern economies. They are simultaneously engines of growth and custodians of systemic stability. While their primary function is to allocate capital efficiently, their operations are deeply intertwined with public trust, regulatory oversight, and macroeconomic resilience. This dual role becomes particularly visible during periods of financial stress, when decisions taken in the pursuit of profitability can amplify vulnerabilities rather than mitigate them. One persistent banking challenge lies in the tension between credit expansion and risk containment. In growth phases, banks are incentivized to loosen lending standards to capture market share, often relying heavily on optimistic projections and asset valuations. Such practices appear rational in isolation but collectively generate fragility. When economic conditions reverse, non-performing assets rise, capital buffers erode, and balance sheets reveal risks that were previously obscured by growth narratives. Regulatory interventions, though designed to prevent systemic collapse, introduce their own complications. Compliance requirements increase operational costs and can constrain lending, particularly to small and medium enterprises. Moreover, regulation often responds to past crises, leaving banks to navigate new financial instruments and digital risks with frameworks that lag innovation. This regulatory asymmetry fuels debates over whether banks are being overburdened or insufficiently restrained. Compounding these issues is the evolving relationship between banks and technology. Digitalization promises efficiency, financial inclusion, and real-time risk monitoring. Yet it also concentrates operational risks, exposes systems to cyber threats, and alters the traditional bank–customer relationship. As banks increasingly resemble technology-driven service platforms, questions arise about accountability, resilience, and the adequacy of existing safeguards. Ultimately, banking stability depends not merely on stronger regulations or advanced technology, but on institutional judgment. Without disciplined risk culture and transparent governance, banks may continue oscillating between excess and restraint, reinforcing cycles of confidence and crisis rather than breaking them.

Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?
options: Technological innovation has eliminated traditional banking risks
Banking crises often emerge from the interaction of incentives and oversight
Regulatory frameworks are sufficient to prevent future financial instability
Digital banking reduces the need for institutional judgment
spmock102.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - Banking crises often emerge from the interaction of incentives and oversight.

Explanation:
The passage implies that excessive risk-taking during growth phases, combined with reactive regulation, creates cycles of vulnerability. Crises arise from this interaction rather than from a single cause.

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG:
A contradicts the passage’s emphasis on new digital risks.
C overstates regulatory effectiveness, which the passage questions.
D is incorrect as institutional judgment is presented as crucial.

spmock102.word:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

options: The safety protocols were examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols were being examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols had been examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
The safety protocols are being examined by the inspectors when the alarm was triggered.
spmock102.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

📌 Rule / Concept: Past Continuous Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Past Continuous tense, the active structure is:
Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + was/were + being + V³ (+ by + Subject)

The word “being” is compulsory in continuous passive constructions. The auxiliary (was/were) must agree with the new subject, and the main verb must be converted into its past participle (V³) form.

Here, “were examining” is in Past Continuous tense.
“The safety protocols” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since it is plural, we use “were”. In continuous passive constructions, “being” must be added after the auxiliary. The verb “examining” changes to its past participle form “examined”.

Hence, “were being examined” is the correct transformation.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

“Being” is mandatory in continuous passive forms.
Use “was” for singular subjects and “were” for plural subjects.
Always convert V-ing to V³ in passive voice.
Do not convert continuous tense into simple past while converting.

spmock103.word:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

During the pre-digital era, travelers _________ rely heavily on physical maps and the kindness of strangers to navigate through the labyrinthine streets of old European cities.
spmock103.explanation:
Replace blank with “used to”.

Rule / Concept: "Used to" (Semi-Modal for Past Habit) –

The modal "used to" is used to describe a habit or a state that existed in the past but is no longer true or does not happen in the present. It is always followed by the base form of the verb (V1). Unlike "be used to," it does not require an auxiliary verb (is/am/are/was/were) when used to denote a discontinued past action.

Application to the Given Question - The sentence sets a past context ("During the pre-digital era"). It describes a habitual action of travelers (relying on maps) that has changed due to the advent of GPS and digital technology. Option (a) "used to" correctly expresses this discontinued habit.

More Examples for Clarity -

  1. I used to play cricket every Sunday when I was in school.

  2. There used to be a famous library at the corner of this street.

Things to Remember/Exam Tips -

  1. V1 check: Always look for the Verb form. "Used to + V1" = Past Habit.

  2. Discontinued Action: Use this rule only when the action has stopped. If the action is still continuing, "used to" is incorrect.

  3. Negative/Interrogative: In negative sentences, we use "did not use to" (not "usedn't" in modern exams). Example: He didn't use to smoke.

spmock103.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Future Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Present Conditional Tense.

Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object) should be converted into Present Conditional (Subject + would + V1 +object).

For example:

He said, "I will be in Kolkata on Friday" (Direct Speech)

He said that he would be in Kolkata on Friday. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the Present Simple verb 'live' will change into Past Simple.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The verb 'will find out' (future simple) is changed into 'would find out' (present conditional).

· The verb 'live' (present simple) is changed into 'lived' (past simple).

· The pronoun 'you' is changed into 'I'.

None of the options except (b) follows these changes. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The officer told me that they would find out where I lived.

spmock104.explanation:
Replace blank with “used”.

Rule/Concept: "Used" as a Main Verb (Action Verb)-

While "used to" is a common semi-modal used to describe past habits, the word "used" on its own often functions as a regular Main Verb (Action Verb). In this capacity, it is the past tense form of the verb "use," meaning "to employ something for a purpose."

Application to the Given Question- In question, the sentence refers to a specific physical action performed by strategists in the past (the act of employing cipher wheels). Unlike "used to," which focuses on a discontinued habit, "used" here acts as a transitive verb with "cipher wheels" as its direct object.

Corrected Sentence- Before the advent of digital encryption, military strategists used cipher wheels to transmit highly classified information across enemy lines.

More Examples for Clarity

  1. I used a calculator for all these complex calculations.

  2. Mohan bought a used car for his wife. (Here, it acts as an adjective/past participle).

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  1. Object Check: If there is a direct object (a noun) immediately following, it is likely the Main Verb "used" (meaning employed).

  2. Context Clue: "Used to" + V1 (base form) is for past habits. "Used" + Noun is for the action of employing a tool.

  3. The "Be" Trap: Avoid adding "is/am/are/was/were" before "used" unless you are describing a state of being accustomed to something or using a passive voice construction.

spmock104.word:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A) I have completed the initial draft of my novel. The editing process will start next week.

B) I have complete the initial draft of my novel. The editing process will start next week.

C) I have completes the initial draft of my novel. The editing process will start next week.

D) I have completed the initial draft of my novel. The editing process will starts next week.
spmock104.explanation:
The grammatically correct sentence is A. The error in sentence B is related to verb form. The phrase "have complete" is incorrect because "complete" is the base form of the verb, whereas the present perfect tense requires the past participle form of the verb. The correct form is "have completed." The verb "complete" should be in the past participle form "completed" to match the present perfect tense of the sentence. The error in sentence C is again related to verb from. The phrase "have completes" is incorrect. The verb "completes" is in the present tense, but the present perfect tense requires the past participle form "completed." The error in sentence D is related to verb form. The phrase "will starts" is incorrect because "starts" is the present tense form, whereas "will" requires the base form of the verb. When using "will" for future tense, the verb that follows should be in its base form, not the third person singular form. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

The phrase "The reason... is because" is a common redundancy in English. The word "reason" implies causality, as does the word "because." Using them together is grammatically superfluous. Option a) is that the main supplier correctly replaces "because" with "that," eliminating the redundancy and forming a grammatically sound sentence.

Option b) is due to the main supplier is also problematic. "Due to" should typically modify a noun, not follow a linking verb like "is" in this structure. For example, "The delay was due to the supplier's failure."

Option c) is on account of the main supplier is grammatically possible but wordy and less direct than "is that...". Also, it would need to be followed by the -ing form of verb "failing".

So, the correct sentence is: The reason for the unexpected project delay is that the main supplier failed to deliver the crucial components on the agreed-upon date, causing a major logistical bottleneck.

spmock105.word:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence.

If I knew his address, I (would have visited his) home to meet his parents.
spmock105.explanation:
This sentence is a Type 2 conditional, used for hypothetical or unreal situations in the present. The 'if' clause uses the Simple Past tense ("knew") to express this unreality. The main clause (the result clause) in a Type 2 conditional must use "would" + the base form of the verb. The underlined segment incorrectly uses "would have visited," which belongs to a Type 3 conditional (for unreal past situations).

The correct option is "would visit his" because it follows the correct structure for a Type 2 conditional ("would" + base verb).

Option b) "will visit his" is used for Type 1 conditionals (real future possibilities).

Option c) "would be visiting his" implies an ongoing action, which is less appropriate here than the simple result.

Option d) "will have visited his" is the Future Perfect tense and doesn't fit the conditional structure.

So, the correct sentence is: If I knew his address, I would visit his home to meet his parents.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is a) would visit his.

spmock105.word: The medical board’s primary requirement is that every resident doctor __________ at least twelve hours of rest between consecutive shifts to ensure patient safety and minimize clinical errors.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Subjunctive (Noun Triggers)

The Present Subjunctive mood is used in "that-clauses" following not only specific verbs and adjectives but also nouns that express a requirement, necessity, or demand (such as requirement, suggestion, recommendation, order, insistence). In this mood, the verb must be in its base form, regardless of the subject's person or number.

💢 Application to the Given Question - The noun requirement followed by "that" triggers the subjunctive mood. Even though the subject "every resident doctor" is singular and would typically take the indicative verb "takes," the presence of the subjunctive trigger requires the base form take.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ The requirement that he be present is non-negotiable.

Example 2 ✅ Her suggestion that the team work on weekends was rejected.

Example 3 ✅ It is a demand of the law that every driver possess a valid license.

that she could have use my car to get away
that she can use my car to get away with

The usage of the word 'use' is incorrect in the underlined part. Either the third form of a verb should be used after the helping verb 'have', or the word 'have' should be removed from the sentence so that the first form of the verb fits appropriately after the modal verb 'could/can' in the sentence. So, options (a) and (c) are incorrect as they do not rectify this error.

Option (d) is incorrect as 'to get away with' means 'to escape'. It does not make the sentence coherent as one cannot escape a place and yet stay in the speaker's hometown.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Note: Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as the possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

The sentence in the Passive voice is in Past Indefinite. So, the sentence in the Active voice should be in Past Indefinite.
