spmock105.word:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The company had implemented corrective measures before the regulator issued the notice.
options: Corrective measures were implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
Corrective measures have been implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
Corrective measures had been implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
Corrective measures were being implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
spmock105.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (C)

📌 Rule / Concept: Past Perfect Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Past Perfect tense, the active structure is:
Subject + had + V³ + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + had + been + V³ (+ by + Subject)

The word “been” is compulsory in Past Perfect passive constructions. The tense must remain Past Perfect after conversion.

Here, “had implemented” is in Past Perfect tense.
“Corrective measures” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since the tense is Past Perfect, we must use “had been” + V³. The verb “implemented” remains in its past participle form.

Hence, “had been implemented” is the correct transformation.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

“Had been” is mandatory in Past Perfect passive voice.
Never change Past Perfect into Simple Past while converting.
The main verb must remain in V³ form.
Check subject–verb agreement even after tense conversion.

spmock105.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form.

She works at the checkout at the local supermarket.
options: She will work at the checkout at the local supermarket.
She is working at the checkout at the local supermarket.
She has worked at the checkout at the local supermarket.
She worked at the checkout at the local supermarket.
spmock105.explanation:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form is (d). Option (d) changes the verb "works" (present tense) to "worked" (simple past tense). The simple past tense is used to talk about actions or events that happened and were completed in the past. It is formed by using the past form of the main verb (in this case, "worked"). Option (a) is in the simple future tense ("will" + base form of the verb). Option (b) is in the present continuous tense ("is" + present participle). Option (c) is in the present perfect tense (has + past participle). Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

has it

📌 Rule / Concept: Negative Meaning Word (“Little”) + Auxiliary Repetition

The word “little” (without “a”) carries a negative meaning (almost none).

When a statement is negative in meaning → the question tag must be positive.

Also, when the main clause contains an auxiliary verb (has/have/is/was etc.), we must repeat that auxiliary in the tag.

💢 Application to the Given Question

  • “Little progress” → negative meaning

  • Therefore → tag must be positive

  • The auxiliary used is has

  • Subject “progress” → replaced by it

So, the correct tag is: has it?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

🧠 Things to Remember

  • “Little” (without “a”) = negative meaning.

  • Negative meaning → positive tag.

  • Repeat the same auxiliary from the main clause.

  • Do not get confused between “a little” (positive meaning) and “little” (negative meaning).

spmock105.word:
Select the passive form of the given sentence:

"The acquisition deal offered the shareholders a 20% premium over the market price."
options: The shareholders were offered a 20% premium over the market price.
A 20% premium was offered to the shareholders over the market price.
A 20% premium was offered the shareholders over the market price.
Both (A) and (B) are correct.
spmock105.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (D)

📌 Rule / Concept: Double Object Verbs – Active to Passive Conversion
When a verb takes two objects (Indirect Object + Direct Object), the passive can be formed in two ways: (1) Indirect object as subject → Indirect Object + was/were + V³ + Direct Object. (2) Direct object as subject → Direct Object + was/were + V³ + to + Indirect Object. The tense must remain unchanged during conversion.

📌 Application to the Given Question

The acquisition deal offered the shareholders a 20% premium over the market price. Here, “offered” is in the simple past tense and takes two objects: “the shareholders” (indirect object) and “a 20% premium” (direct object). Passive Form 1: “The shareholders were offered a 20% premium over the market price.” Passive Form 2: “A 20% premium was offered to the shareholders over the market price.” Both structures are grammatically correct. Option (C) omits the required preposition “to” when the direct object becomes the subject, making it incorrect.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Verbs like give, offer, send, teach allow two passive forms. If the direct object becomes the subject, use “to” (or “for,” depending on the verb). Maintain the original tense. Check whether both options are grammatically correct before selecting one.

📌 Rule / Concept: “Need” + Gerund / Passive Infinitive Structure
When a sentence contains need + V-ing (e.g., needs renovating), it carries a passive meaning. It can be transformed into the structure: Subject + needs + to be + V³. The gerund form after “need” implies necessity in a passive sense. However, “needs being + V³” is grammatically incorrect in standard English.

📌 Application to the Given Question

The correct equivalent passive structure is: “needs to be renovated.” Option (A) is incorrect because “to renovate” makes the subject perform the action. Option (C) is grammatically incorrect (“needs being renovated”). Therefore, Option (B) is the accurate passive form.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

“Need + V-ing” often carries passive meaning. The correct expanded form is “need(s) to be + V³.” Avoid structures like “needs being + V³.” Ensure the subject is not shown performing the action if the meaning is passive.

spmock106.word: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

Option (a) is not correct. After the modal verb "must," we use the base form of the verb ("find"). But 'found' (past tense form) is not the base form. Modal verbs like "must" express necessity or obligation and are always followed by the base form of the main verb. So, 'found' should be replaced with the base form 'find'. Option (b) is not correct. After the modal verb "must," we use the base form of the verb ("prioritise"). But 'prioritises' (present tense form) is not the base form. Modal verbs such as "must" indicate necessity and are followed by the base form of the verb that expresses the action required. So, 'prioritises' should be replaced with the base form 'prioritise'. The correct sentence is: We must prioritise customer satisfaction in our business strategy.

Option (d) is incorrect as well. After the modal verb "will," we use the base form of the verb ("call"). Modal verbs like "will" express future actions or intentions and are followed by the base form of the main verb. But 'called' (past tense form) is not the base form. So, we should replace 'called' with the base form 'call'. The correct sentence is: He will call you as soon as he gets home from work. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

spmock106.word:

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

For example:

She said that Yusuf had sent her a letter. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
told... thatsaid to

spmock106.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the positive degree of comparison:

This is the largest tree in the park.
options: No other tree in the park is as large as this one.

In the park, this tree is larger than other trees.
spmock106.explanation:
The original sentence, "This is the largest tree in the park," is in the superlative degree of comparison. To transform it into a positive degree, we must ensure the sentence uses "as...as" to indicate comparison without implying comparative or superlative status.

Option a) is correct. It uses the positive degree ("as large as") and compares this tree to other trees in the park without explicitly stating it is the largest.

Options b) and c) are in the superlative degrees, while option d) is in the comparative degree.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

spmock107.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present tense form.

We received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
options: We will be receiving a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We have received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We had received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We were receiving a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
spmock107.explanation:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in present tense form is (b). Option (b) changes the verb "received" (past tense) to "have received" (present perfect tense). The present perfect tense is used to talk about actions that were completed at some unspecified time before the present moment and have relevance to the present. It is formed using the auxiliary verb "have" (or "has" for singular subjects) followed by the past participle of the main verb (in this case, "received"). Option (a) is in the future continuous tense ("will be" + present participle of the verb). Option (c) is in the past perfect tense ("had" + past participle of the verb). Option (d) is in the past continuous tense ("were"/ "was" + present participle of the verb). Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

The infinitive marker 'To' is always followed by a base form of the verb, so the use of 'made/makes/making' [V2/V3, V5, V4 respectively] will be incorrect here. NOTE/-

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below: Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground. Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion. The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

In formal competitive exam English, collective nouns such as board, committee, jury, panel are generally treated as singular unless emphasis is on individual members.

spmock108.word:
Identify the passive form:

"It is necessary that the regulatory body implement the new KYC norms immediately."
options: It is necessary that the new KYC norms are implemented immediately.
It is necessary that the new KYC norms be implemented immediately.
The new KYC norms are necessary to be implemented immediately.
The regulatory body is necessary to implement the new KYC norms.
spmock108.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

📌 Rule / Concept: Subjunctive Mood (Mandative Construction) – Active to Passive Conversion

When expressions like it is necessary that, it is essential that, it is important that are followed by a clause, the verb in that-clause takes the base form (subjunctive mood). In passive construction, the structure becomes: It + is + adjective + that + object + be + V³. The word “be” is used instead of “is/are” because the clause remains in the subjunctive form.

📌 Application to the Given Question

It is necessary that the regulatory body implement the new KYC norms immediately. Here, “implement” is in the subjunctive base form (not “implements”). In passive voice, “the new KYC norms” becomes the subject of the that-clause. Since the sentence is mandative/subjunctive, we use “be implemented” (not “are implemented”). Hence, “It is necessary that the new KYC norms be implemented immediately” is the correct transformation. Option (A) incorrectly uses the indicative “are implemented.” Options (C) and (D) distort the structure and meaning.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

After expressions of necessity, demand, suggestion, use the base verb (subjunctive). In passive subjunctive, use “be + V³,” not “is/are.” Do not shift to the indicative mood. Preserve the original structure carefully.

Rule/Concept: Dare as a Semi-Modal (Negative/Interrogative)-

"Dare" (meaning to have enough courage) behaves as a semi-modal verb primarily in negative sentences and questions. Like "Need," when it acts as a modal:

  1. It is Subject-Neutral: It does not take's' even with third-person singular or plural subjects.

  2. It takes a Bare Infinitive: It is followed by V1 without the preposition "to".

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, "dare" is used in the negative form ("dare not"). Even though the subject "divers" is plural (which would take 'dare' anyway), the key identifier is the word "venture" (V1) appearing immediately after without "to". If "dare" were a main verb, the sentence would require: "do not dare to venture." Since the "to" is missing, "dare" must be the modal form.

Correct Usage -

  1. He dare not speak against the master. (Modal)

  2. How dare you open my mail? (Interrogative Modal)

  3. He dares to challenge the champion. (Main verb - note the 's' and 'to')

Incorrect Usage

  1. She dares not go out in the dark. (Incorrect modal form; should be 'dare') ❌

  2. dare not to touch the wire. (Incorrect; 'to' is not used with modal dare) ❌

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  1. The "How Dare You" Check: We never say "How dares you" or "How dare you to." This is the easiest way to remember that 'dare' as a modal drops 's' and 'to'.

  2. The "Not" Trigger: If you see 'not' immediately after the blank, prioritize the modal form (No 's', No 'to').

  3. Main Verb Substitution: If the sentence uses "do/does/did," then 'dare' is a main verb and must take "to" (e.g., He does not dare to go).

spmock109.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in positive degree of comparison.

She is the dullest child in the class.
options: She is very duller in the class.
Dullest child in the class is she.
No other child in the class is as dull as she.
In the class of all she is dull.
spmock109.explanation:
The option that expresses the given sentence in the positive degree of comparison is 'No other child in the class is as dull as she'. The given sentence is already in the superlative degree, indicating the highest degree of dullness. To express it in the positive degree, which denotes a basic or straightforward comparison without emphasising the extremeness, the sentence can rephrased as: "No other child in the class is as dull as she." This construction compares the dullness of the specified child to the dullness of the other children in the class without singling her out as the "dullest." It represents a positive degree of comparison by highlighting a level of dullness without making it the most extreme in the class.

Option (a) contains a grammatical error with "very duller," as "duller" already implies a comparative degree. The correct form would be either "She is very dull in the class" or "She is duller than others in the class."

Option (b) maintains the superlative form "dullest," which is not in the positive degree. It still emphasises the extremeness.

Option (d) has an awkward and less conventional structure. It does not clearly convey a positive degree of comparison.

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

spmock109.word:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

I played a paradox on my sister by hiding fake spiders in her room.
spmock109.explanation:
The word "paradox" doesn't accurately convey the intended meaning in the context of the sentence. A "paradox" is a concept or statement that seems contradictory or goes against common belief, yet it might be true or logical within a specific context. In contrast, the sentence implies that the speaker played a trick or a practical joke on his/her sister by hiding fake spiders in her room. This action aligns more with the concept of a "prank" rather than a "paradox." A prank involves a playful or mischievous act intended to trick, amuse, or surprise someone, typically in a light-hearted manner. Accordingly, 'prank' is a suitable word to replace 'paradox'. 'Foul' refers to something that is offensive, unpleasant, or morally unacceptable. However, in the context of the sentence, the act of hiding fake spiders as a joke on the sister doesn't necessarily imply anything offensive or morally wrong. Therefore, "foul" doesn't appropriately replace "paradox" in this context. A 'riddle' is a type of puzzle or enigmatic question that requires thought or cleverness to solve. However, the sentence is describing an action, not a puzzle or a question posed to someone. So, "riddle" isn't the appropriate replacement for "paradox" in this context. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The revised sentence is: I played a prank on my sister by hiding fake spiders in her room.

spmock110.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

He said, "My friend wrote me a letter."
options: He said that his friend had written him a letter.
He said that his friend has written him a letter.
He said that my friend had written him a letter.
He said that his friend wrote him a letter.
spmock110.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

For example:

He said, "Arya sent me a book." (Direct Speech)

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"Said" will change to "said that".

"My" will change to "his".

"Wrote" will change to "had written".

"Me" will change to "him".

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): He said that his friend had written him a letter.

The book that we had sent him yesterday would have been read by him.
The book that we sent him yesterday will have been read by him.
The book that we have sent him yesterday will be read by him.
spmock110.explanation:
The subject of the Active voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. The object of the Active voice is changed into subject of the Passive voice. The usage of a 'to be' form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

Preposition "by" is used before the object made in passive voice.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Perfect tense. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Perfect tense.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will have sent that mail. (Active voice)

That mail will have been sent by him. (Passive voice)

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

spmock110.word:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The organization offered the candidate a senior position in the compliance division.
options: The candidate was offered a senior position in the compliance division
A senior position was offered the candidate in the compliance division.
A senior position was offered to the candidate in the compliance division.
Both A and C
spmock110.explanation:
The Correct Ans is Option (D)

📌 Rule / Concept: Double Object Verbs in Passive Voice

Certain verbs such as give, offer, send, tell, award, lend, promise, etc., take two objects:

Subject + Verb + Indirect Object (person) + Direct Object (thing)

In passive voice, either object can become the subject. Therefore, double object verbs allow two correct passive forms.

Structure 1 (Indirect Object as Subject):
Indirect Object + be + V³ + Direct Object

Structure 2 (Direct Object as Subject):
Direct Object + be + V³ + to + Indirect Object

💢 Application to the Given Question- Here:

Indirect Object = the candidate
Direct Object = a senior position

Passive Form 1: The candidate was offered a senior position in the compliance division.

Passive Form 2: A senior position was offered to the candidate in the compliance division.

Since both structures are grammatically correct, the correct answer is Option (D) Both A and C.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Double object verbs allow two passive structures. When the direct object becomes subject, “to” is usually required before the indirect object. Banking and SSC Mains frequently test whether candidates know that both structures are grammatically correct.

spmock110.word:
Modern societies often celebrate progress through visible indicators—economic growth, technological penetration, and expanding infrastructure—while quietly overlooking fractures that resist quantification. Social inequality, though frequently acknowledged in rhetoric, is often treated as an abstract concern rather than a lived reality. The persistence of unequal access to education, healthcare, and legal recourse reveals that disparity is not merely a residual flaw of development but, in many cases, its unintended companion. Progress, when unevenly distributed, can deepen the very divides it claims to bridge. Public discourse tends to individualize social failure. Poverty is reframed as lack of effort, marginalization as absence of adaptability, and exclusion as personal deficiency. Such narratives offer moral comfort to the privileged by converting structural disadvantage into personal responsibility. Over time, this framing dulls collective urgency. When inequality is perceived as self-inflicted, social empathy is replaced by conditional sympathy—extended only to those deemed “deserving.” Institutions, meanwhile, respond with procedural solutions that emphasize efficiency over equity. Welfare systems grow increasingly conditional, access mechanisms become more complex, and accountability is measured through compliance rather than outcome. While these approaches appear neutral, they disproportionately burden those already navigating scarcity. The result is a paradoxical system in which assistance exists formally but remains functionally inaccessible to many. The most corrosive consequence of persistent inequality is not material deprivation alone but the erosion of social trust. When large sections of society experience the state as distant or indifferent, civic engagement weakens and resentment quietly accumulates. Addressing social issues, therefore, requires more than policy expansion; it demands a recalibration of how societies assign blame, distribute dignity, and define progress itself.

The tone of the passage is best described as:
options: Moralistic and accusatory toward privileged social groups
Analytical and critically reflective of systemic inequality
Neutral and descriptive of socio-economic conditions
Optimistic about institutional capacity for reform
spmock110.explanation:
The Correct Answer is - Analytical and critically reflective of systemic inequality.

Explanation:
The passage systematically examines how inequality is framed, managed, and normalized without emotional condemnation. The author maintains a reflective and critical tone, emphasizing structural patterns rather than assigning direct blame.

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG:
A is incorrect because the passage critiques narratives, not individuals.
C is misleading as the passage clearly evaluates consequences and assumptions.
D is wrong since the passage remains cautious and does not express optimism.

This sentence uses the appropriate definite article 'the' before the words 'warrior' and 'lion', indicating specific individuals or entities. Additionally, it correctly uses the phrase 'the right time'. The phrase 'the right time' is the correct choice because it refers to a particular moment that the warrior is waiting for. Using 'an right time' is grammatically incorrect as 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Options (a), (c), and (d) contain grammatical errors. In option (a), 'an right time' should be 'the right time'. Similarly, options (c) and (d) have similar errors with the use of "an" instead of "the" before the words "warrior" and "lion."

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

An article is a word that comes before a noun to indicate whether it's specific or general.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

spmock112.word:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The Three Musketeers _______ often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.
spmock112.explanation:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B). Replace the blank with "is".

Rule/Concept: Titles as Abstract Singular Entities:

In English, names of books, movies, countries, or organizations are treated as singular proper nouns. Even if the title contains a plural noun (Musketeers) or a number (Three), it represents one single entity (one story).

The "Article A" Anchor: In complex sentences, look for the phrase "a prime example." The use of the singular article "a" later in the sentence is a dead giveaway that the subject must be singular.

Proper Noun Identification: Words that are capitalized in the middle of a sentence (The Three Musketeers) are usually titles. Treat them as a single "IT," not "THEY."

Common Traps: Watch out for similar titles like Gulliver's Travels, Hard Times, The Arabian Nights, or The United Nations. All of these take a singular verb.

Elimination Strategy: If you see a singular complement (like "a prime example"), immediately eliminate all plural verb options.

Why "Was" (Option C) is incorrect here: If you choose "was," you are implying that the book used to be cited as an example in the past, but it is no longer considered one today. Since the literary status of a masterpiece is usually a continuous fact, the present tense "is" is the grammatically superior choice.

Adverbs of Frequency: Words like "often," "usually," "generally," and "always" are strong signals that the examiner is testing you on the Simple Present Tense.

Correct Sentence: The Three Musketeers is often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.

Next, R, "but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued," contrasts with S. Finally, P, "and the learned man has been held in higher esteem," connects to the ending.

The order Q-S-R-P forms: "India has been a land of learning through the ages, not indeed in the sense that education has been universal, but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued, and the learned man has been held in higher esteem than the warrior or the administrator."

Option 2 is correct.

spmock112.word: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The quietest member of your family has a truly brilliant idea.
This responsibility place a particular burden on two men.
The products we source from them is not connected to the livestock industry.
It take courage to open yourself up to scrutiny again.
spmock112.explanation:
The sentence given in option (a) is grammatically correct.

Option (b) is not correct. The error is related to the subject-verb agreement issue. The verb "place" (plural) is incorrect. The subject "This responsibility" is singular, so the verb should also be singular. "Places" is the correct third-person singular form of the verb "place."

The correct form should be "places" to agree with the subject "This responsibility," which is singular. The correct sentence is: This responsibility places a particular burden on two men.

Option (c) is incorrect. The error is related to the subject-verb agreement issue. The verb "is" is incorrect. The subject "products" is plural, so the verb "are" (plural) should be used instead of "is" (singular) to maintain subject-verb agreement. The correct sentence is: The products we source from them are not connected to the livestock industry.

Option (d) is also incorrect. The error is related to the subject-verb agreement issue. The plural verb "take" is incorrect. The subject "It" is singular, so the verb should also be singular. The correct form should be "takes" (singular) to agree with the singular subject "It." The correct sentence is: It takes courage to open yourself up to scrutiny again. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

However, "broadly" is not the most suitable adverb to convey the sound of thunder during a storm. The word "loudly" is the most appropriate substitution for "broadly" in this context. "Loudly" more accurately describes the nature of thunder during a storm, indicating that the thunder produced a strong, powerful sound that could be heard over a wide area. The word "patiently" means to act with patience or tolerance, especially in dealing with delays or difficulties. However, in the context of the sentence describing thunder during a storm, "patiently" does not appropriately convey the nature of the sound or the manner in which the thunder roared. "Sensibly" means acting with good judgment or practicality. This word also doesn't accurately describe the sound or manner of the thunder during the storm. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

spmock112.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Each candidate was making tall promises.
options: Tall promises were being made by each candidate.
Tall promises are made by each candidate.
Tall promises will be made by each candidate.
Tall promises are being made by each candidate.
spmock112.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

The options except (1) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

spmock112.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech:

Kanhaiya said to me, "Do you want to sing?"
options: Kanhaiya enquires if I want to sing.
Kanhaiya said that whether I would sing.
Kanhaiya said that I would sing or not.
Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing.
spmock112.explanation:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Simple Present tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Simple Past tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Said to-Asked/enquired

Do-If

Accordingly, the sentence that follows the above rules of Indirect speech is "Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing."

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

spmock112.word:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

A group of students _______ studying in the library.
spmock112.explanation:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D)- Replace the blank with "is".

Rule/Concept: Collective Nouns with Indefinite Articles Changing "The" to "A" does not change the fundamental rule of subject-verb agreement for collective nouns. Whether it is "The group" or "A group," the word "group" remains a singular collective noun representing one single unit.

Subject Focus: The subject is "group" (singular), not "students" (plural). The phrase "of students" is simply providing more information about the group.

Common Phrases following this rule: A pack of wolves is, A bunch of keys is, A team of players is, A fleet of ships is.

Correct Sentence: A group of students is studying in the library.

spmock112.word:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

"Either the lead engineers or the project director _________ expected to deliver the final presentation to the board of investors this afternoon."
spmock112.explanation:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B)

The singular verb "is" is required because the noun closest to the blank is singular.

Rule/Concept: The Proximity Rule (Either... or) When two subjects are joined by "Either... or" (or Neither... nor), the verb does not care about the first subject. It must agree strictly with the nearest subject (the one right before the blank).

Logic Breakdown:

Subject 1: "The lead engineers" (Plural).

Subject 2: "The project director" (Singular).

The Decision: Since "director" is the neighbour closest to the blank, the verb must be singular.

Correct Sentence: Either the lead engineers or the project director is expected to deliver the final presentation...

spmock112.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Why was Shekhar not taken seriously by any of the team members?
options: Why do any of the team members not take Shekhar seriously?
Why didn't any of the team members take Shekhar seriously?
Why will any of the team members not take Shekhar seriously?
Why does any of the team members not take Shekhar Kapoor seriously?
spmock112.explanation:
•The above sentence is an interrogative sentence starting with a question word (why, when, how, where, etc.).

The subject and object of the passive sentence should become the object and subject of the active sentence respectively.

While making the sentence active, we need to put the suitable helping verb after the question word according to the new subject.

Use the correct form of the main verb according to the tense instead of the past participle.

Remove preposition ‘by’.

•Use the following syntax for the above sentence-

Passive voice- Question word + was/were + subject + not + V3 + by + object + other + ?

Active voice - Question word + did not + new subject + V3 + new object + other + ?

Hence, the correct active voice form is 'Why didn't any of the team members take Shekhar seriously?'

Hence, option b) is correct.

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verbs ['are' and 'is'] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

In such questions, the preposition is kept intact with the verb while transforming the sentence into Passive Voice.

The Passive form of the sentence is: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + 'to be' + V3 + Preposition + by + Object.

Some verbs that have their prepositions intact in Passive voice: Look at, look down upon, look after, laugh at, smile at, enquired into, ignorant of.

Also, the sentence is in the Present Indefinite tense in the Active voice. So, in the Passive voice, Present indefinite tense should be used.
